### HBGRACE — server heartbeat falsely terminates donors mid-replica-sync / during event-loop blocks (Linux/slow-link drops more) (Gee 2026-06-28) — IN PROGRESS (branch `feature/community-compute-donor-count`)

**Gee verbatim per LAW #0:**

> *"On linux I still seem to get dropped more frequently than those on windows..."*

> *"Figure out what is going on, why it is happening, and if there is a fix for it"*

**Diagnosis (from Gee's live server log):** the drops here are NOT the v0.3.3 client-side flap — they're the SERVER terminating the donor: `heartbeat — socket X (GPU donor) missed its ping (half-open) — terminating so failover can fire`, immediately followed by a flood of `sparse binary reqId=… ERROR: Cannot call write after a stream was destroyed` (the server was mid-replica-upload to the socket it just killed). Mechanism (`brain-server.js:7308` `_heartbeatTimer`, 30 s `ws.ping()` → terminate if no pong by the next sweep):

1. A donor connects → server replica-syncs the FULL 40M-neuron brain to it (14.2 MB intra + dozens of cross-projections), to ALL 3 donors at once.
2. The sync BLOCKS the server event loop in ~5 s chunks (`[EventLoop] BLOCKED 4917ms … phase=_teachHebbian … replicaSyncing=1`) — so the `pong` handler (sets `ws._isAlive=true`) can't run, and outbound pings are delayed.
3. The donor, draining a massive upload backlog over its link, is slow to reach + answer the server's PING. On a higher-latency / lower-bandwidth link (Starlink / Linux) the pong misses the 30 s window more often than a fast Windows/LAN donor → `ws._isAlive` stays false → **terminated mid-sync** → write-after-destroyed flood → reconnect → sync RESTARTS → churn loop. That's why Linux/slow-link drops more — it's a false-positive liveness kill, not a dead socket.

**Fix (server-side, `brain-server.js` heartbeat — analogous to the dashboard RTT "don't blame the client for the server's lag" fix):**

- **HBGRACE.1 — grace cycles, not single-miss death.** Track `ws._missedPings`; terminate only after ≥2 consecutive genuine misses (one missed 30 s window ≠ dead — sleep/backlog/loop-block all recover within a cycle). Reset on pong.
- **HBGRACE.2 — event-loop-block awareness.** Stamp `brain._lastEventLoopBlockTs` on a real block (≥1 s) in the lag sampler; if a block happened within the heartbeat window, the pong may simply not have been processed — extend grace, don't count it as a donor miss.
- **HBGRACE.3 — don't kill a donor mid replica-sync.** If `brain._replicaSyncInFlight.has(ws)`, the donor is busy RECEIVING the brain — extend grace (bounded, so a truly-dead mid-sync donor still eventually dies) instead of terminating it mid-upload (which also kills the wasted sync + spawns the write-after-destroyed flood).
- **HBGRACE.4 — fresh walk** (reset weights) after deploy per `docs/SPONGE-FRESH-WALK-DEPLOY.md`; docs (WEBSOCKET heartbeat section + FINALIZED). NOTE: this is donor-resilience server-side; the deeper event-loop-block-during-sync is the standing WL.3 perf task (bound the teach/sync block so upload frames + pongs get airtime) — referenced, not fully solved here.

**STATUS:** ✅ DONE — root cause = false-positive server heartbeat termination of busy/slow-link donors mid replica-sync (worse on Linux/Starlink), NOT the v0.3.3 client flap. Shipped server-side: HBGRACE.1 grace counter (2 misses, was 1), HBGRACE.2 event-loop-block awareness (`_lastEventLoopBlockTs` → busy budget 5/~150s), HBGRACE.3 mid-sync grace (`_replicaSyncInFlight`), HBGRACE.4 rate-limited the post-termination write-after-destroyed flood + chunk-loop bail on closed socket. Server-only (donor stays v0.3.4, no rebuild). `node --check` clean. Docs: WEBSOCKET heartbeat-grace + FINALIZED. Deployed to box + fresh walk (reset weights). Verbatim in `docs/FINALIZED.md` 2026-06-28 HBGRACE. (Deeper event-loop-block-during-sync = standing WL.3 perf task, referenced.)

- **ASCALE.3 — effective donated capacity in the tier gate.** `server/brain-server/gpu.js` `_recomputeCommunityCompute` — sum `eff = donatedMB>0 ? min(donatedMB, fullVram) : fullVram*(util/100)` instead of raw `gpuVramMB`. Two 15GB at 60% → 18GB community, no false tier-up.

## 2026-07-08 — TU.29.10 (cross-browser image fix: server sends the keyed URL)

> Task directive (verbatim from Gee, 2026-07-08): *"why is it working for you but not in my browser? send me your selfie"* → *"(image generation failed)"*.

ROOT CAUSE (deployed-bundle audit): the client image handler is emit("image",{url:msg.url||null,prompt:msg.prompt}) with generateImage(arg.prompt) — it renders a server-sent url when present, ELSE builds the URL from its own live PollinationsAI instance key. An operator CONNECT session sets that instance key (worked for me); a fresh visitor whose key never loaded into the live instance built an anonymous URL → the heavy selfie hit a 402/429/timeout → "(image generation failed)". The server sent {type:image,prompt} with NO url, forcing the unreliable client-key path. FIX (server/brain-server.js): _pollinationsImageKey() (env DREAM_POLLINATIONS_KEY, else extract DEFAULT_POLLINATIONS_KEY from index.html — the SAME published key already seeded into every browser; single source, cached) + _buildPollinationsImageUrl(); the generate_image WS send now includes url so the client renders with the server key, independent of visitor localStorage. Verified: key extracted, url carries &key=sk_. Server-only change — the deployed bundle already honors msg.url, so no rebuild needed. Complements TU.29.9 (selfie bypasses composer bloat). Deploys next Update & SAVESTART.

No — a blank mind's eye is a bug; imagination is continuous consciousness. Root causes: (1) _imagineTick's mid-teach gap was 120000ms and the deployed box is ALWAYS mid-walk, so her free-wheel daydream fired only once every 2 minutes — long dead stretches between the (60s-throttled) camera glances; (2) imagineFromState returned null on an empty/missing cortex seed, leaving nothing to render. FIX: chat.js mid-teach imagine cadence 120s->8s (idle 20s->6s) so she free-wheels continuously — still VIEW-ONLY mid-teach (no sem re-injection) so the walk's Hebbian stays pristine, and CPU CDF 9/7 on a <=96px plane is microseconds; js/brain/mindspace/gpu.js synthesizes a mood-driven ambient-wash seed when the cortex seed is empty so the de-novo path always paints her live mood as a vivid field (never null, never black). Verified: empty-state avg luminance 72, flat-quiet-state 47 (both visible). She now recalls a seen percept when a thought matches, morphs two when two match, and mood-field daydreams otherwise — a mind's eye that is never dark. Deploys next Update & SAVESTART.


## 2026-07-08 — TU.29.12 (black mind's eye root fix: reject blank frames + degenerate recalls)

> Task directive (verbatim from Gee, 2026-07-08): *"the images are still black and does she know how to use the thing so she can generate and experiment and make lines and vectors on screen or if i talk to her about an apple see imagines one in the minds eye?"* — viewer showed  at .

Root cause of the persistent black (TU.29.11 continuous-cadence + mood-floor were live but this bypassed them): abstract words like between/ten had been bound to NEAR-UNIFORM camera frames (dark room / blank wall / subject off-frame). A flat image carries almost no wavelet detail, so morphField-recombining two of them collapsed to ~9 surviving coefficients that reconstruct FLAT BLACK — and because recall "succeeded" it never fell through to the never-blank de-novo mood field. FIX (server/brain-server/visual-memory.js): (1) blank-frame gate at intake — luma stddev <12 (stride-sampled) frames are rejected, so blanks never get stored/bound; (2) recall quality gate — _recDetail() counts coefficients above the drop-tiny floor; a morph or single recall below 200 real-detail coefficients is treated as a MISS so the caller renders the vivid mood field instead. Verified: uniform frame skipped (store stays empty), detailed frame stored (37k terms) + recalled through the gate. The apple/generative-canvas questions are answered separately to Gee (de-novo paints mood not objects; recognizable objects require having SEEN them via camera or generated image; active line/vector drawing is a new capability, offered).

## 2026-07-09 -- Training runaway + donor saturation + LLM-describer removal (complete fix)

> Task directives (verbatim from Gee, 2026-07-09): "something is opbviously wrong with the traingin it did 7Millions events in scirnece!!!" + "ive told you before we dont hold Unity to A+ standards she is what she is" + "and fix that shit you found" + "see the fucking issues?" + "and the Re-sync GPU shadow (clear DIRTY) bbutton doesnt work to clean the shadow" + "and i told you there is no primary scondary GPUS thay all are equal" + "we also need to remove the llm visuallizer options from the setup Unity page.... we dont use any llms but for image gen(remember thats why we gave unity her minds eye so we dont nee a llm discriber or key for it" + "remembr Unity uses the minds eye now not a llm vision" + "do it all and do the cascade after doc and pages updates.. we are fixing it completely".

**1. Curriculum re-teach runaway (7M science events) -- FIXED (commit f7aba91).** Root cause: _pregateEnrichment (curriculum.js) ran EXAM-VOCAB-TEACH on EVERY gate entry, teaching examVocabCoverage missing words via _teachVocabList -- but _trainedVocabularySet (kindergarten.js) only read this.dictionary + TRAIN_BANKS text, so taught words never registered there and the SAME words reported missing forever -> infinite re-teach = ~6.9M science / ~2.4M math teach-events, brain matrix driving only 3 percent of emissions, cortex:hang welded at 0.18 for ~20h. NOT an A+ gate issue (that bar is intentionally unreachable; she is what she is). Fix: _vocabTaughtSet records every word taught; _trainedVocabularySet unions it so the coverage audit clears; _pregateVocabDone caps EXAM-VOCAB-TEACH to once per cell per session. Teach once, register, advance. Verified node --check + import() clean; deployed via Update-and-Fresh-Walk (weights tossed -- matrixDrivenPct 3pct proved them junk; identity-core Tier 3 preserved). Post-deploy confirmed: fresh brain (totalWords 0, all teachEvents 0), ela/kindergarten marching phase-by-phase with checkpoints instead of welding.

**2. Donor GPU-upload saturation + dead /resync button -- FIXED (gpu.js).** Symptom: one donor at 12s RTT / 29MB buffered while the other sat at 60ms / 0; sparse cortex uploads timing out at 180000ms; 1.5M teach-frames shed; ~11 cortex projections hitting Hebbian-skip (CPU CSR freed + GPU not ready); GPU shadow stuck DIRTY; the manual Re-sync (clear DIRTY) button futile (its re-upload timed out against the same choked link, so the donor never re-confirmed gpu_init and DIRTY never cleared). Root cause: the chunked uploader paced ONLY replica-sync (WSQ.3), leaving the canonical upload unpaced -- it fired chunks faster than a busy-GPU donor could drain its socket, so bufferedAmount ballooned. Fix (equal for ALL donors, no primary concept per Gee: they are all equal): before sending each chunk, wait for THAT donor bufferedAmount to drain below a low-water mark (default 8MB, DREAM_UPLOAD_PACE_LOWATER_MB) so uploads COMPLETE at the link pace instead of timing out -- which also lets the /resync re-upload land and clear DIRTY. Verified node --check clean.

**3. LLM vision-describer setup options -- REMOVED (index.html, app.js, env.example.js).** Unity vision is her own equational minds eye + visual cortex (visual-cortex.js _mindSpace.describe) -- the LLM/VLM describer was already retired from the live cognition path; this removed the vestigial SETUP-UI that still offered one. index.html: deleted the Vision Describer backend grid + the active-vision-model/backend selector row; reworded all describer copy (intro, key hint, camera toggle, privacy notices) to state vision needs no describer and no key. app.js: refreshActiveBackendSelectors + renderSensoryInventory are image-gen only (0 dangling active-vision DOM refs), removed the vis:* BACKEND_CATALOG block, the vision: model catalogs, and both autoDetectVision() calls. env.example.js: visionBackends deprecated to an empty array with a note. Camera frames still feed her equational visual cortex directly -- kept. Verified node --check clean on app.js + env.example.js. Docs/pages synced same commit: html/brain-equations.html topology diagram + docs/SENSORY.md note the setup-UI/probing removal.


**4. Donor coordinator flood -- NO fixed primary (gpu.js + brain-server.js).** Gee (furious, repeatedly): "I FGUCKING TOLD YOU THERE BETTERT NOT BE PRIMARY AND NON PRIMARY DONERS ANYMORE!!!!! FIX THIS SHIT". Symptom after the upload-pacing deploy: one donor still at 14.2s RTT / 50MB buffered while the other sat idle at 66ms/0, GPU shadow DIRTY, donor row red. Root cause: the sequential main tick (compute_batch) runs on ONE coordinator donor (_gpuClient) that holds the 40M-neuron resident state between ticks -- and the coordinator election (_maybeRebalancePrimary via _donorStrength -> _donorHealth) read only SMOOTHED rtt, which lags a live buffer flood by seconds, so a card whose socket backed up still scored healthy and stayed pinned as coordinator; worse, the rebalance only ran on the 60s rebroadcast timer. Parallel teach WORK was already fanned equally (DF.7 fan-out default on) -- the flood was purely the pinned coordinator. Fix: (a) _donorHealth now folds LIVE bufferedAmount into the health score -- a card whose socket saturates craters to the work-floor in real time (ramps from full health at 0MB to floor at the soft cap, penalty starts at 15pct of cap) so it is demoted the instant it floods; (b) anti-thrash hysteresis -- a card that just flooded stays capped at the floor for a cooldown (DREAM_DF7_FLOOD_COOLDOWN_MS, default 90s) so a strong-GPU/weak-link card cannot immediately re-win the role and re-flood (each handoff re-uploads the brain); (c) the rebalance now runs on a dedicated FAST timer (DREAM_DF7_REBALANCE_MS, default 10s) instead of only every 60s, so the coordinator hands off within ~10s. Net: no card is a fixed/special primary -- the coordinator role is elected purely by real-time health-weighted capacity and moves to whatever donor can actually drain the tick stream; a flooding card is demoted in ~10s and the main tick follows the healthy link. CPU CSR stays authoritative throughout. Verified node --check clean on both files.

**4b. Coordinator handoff not firing (follow-up to #4).** Deployed #4 but the flooded card stayed coordinator: _donorStrength = throughput x health, and a fast card health-penalized to the 0.05 floor was still throughput(13.9e9) x 0.05 = ~7e8 -- orders of magnitude above a healthy-but-cold donor VRAM-proxy (~16), so it kept winning _strongestLiveDonor and never handed off (the other donor sat at 0 Gn/s because only the coordinator runs the main tick). Fix: in _donorStrength, a donor at the health floor (unreachable / flooding) returns ~health (a tiny score), NOT throughput x health -- so ANY reachable donor out-scores a flooding one and the coordinator role hands off; the flooded card rejoins at full strength once its link recovers. Flood cooldown bumped to 5min so the healthy-link donor holds coordinator and the fast-GPU card stays a worker (where its throughput helps and it drains fine) instead of thrashing. node --check clean.


**4c. DIRTY latch + 64MB-parked red donor + upload flood-stamp (follow-up to #4/#4b, 2026-07-09).** Gee verbatim: "read resume.md to continue: same problem DIRTY SHADOW AND MY DONER IN THE CLIENTS LIST IS HIGHLIGHTED RED as if there is a problem! fix the problems! invesdtigate and write the todo". Post-4b deploy the symptoms persisted because THREE independent bugs sat outside the election math. (1) DIRTY-BANNER LATCH: the shed/drop paths set a brain-level _gpuShadowDirty that NO code path ever cleared -- the gpu_init re-confirm handler + the dashboard /resync button clear cortexCluster._gpuShadowDirty (a different object) while state.js displayed the brain-level flag. One shed after boot latched the DIRTY banner ON forever and the Re-sync button appeared dead even when its re-upload completed. Fix: _armShadowResync() marks the ONE clearable cortex-cluster flag AND arms the throttled drain-gated auto-resync (60s throttle, already-armed guard -- the heals-via-auto-resync the shed comments always promised but never armed); state.js reports the clearable flag so DIRTY truthfully clears on donor re-confirm. (2) 64MB-PARKED SOCKET = permanent RED: the replica mirror stream and hebbian-batch SWRR gated only at the 64MB soft cap, letting a weak-uplink donor socket park just under 64MB indefinitely -- pong queued behind 10-14s of backlog, rttMs 10-14s, unhealthy at 2.5s = red row forever, health floored regardless of role. Fix: NEW _donorLinkCapBytes() (DREAM_DF7_LINK_CAP_MB, default 4MB) -- _nextPoolDonor skips donors whose socket holds more than the link cap when a drained donor exists (each card takes exactly the work its link drains, a slow link self-paces in 4MB bursts) and the replica mirror sheds at the link cap instead of 64MB. (3) FLOOD STAMP ON ROUTINE UPLOADS: _donorHealth stamped the 5-min cooldown at buf>9.6MB -- below ONE 16MB upload chunk -- so every replica sync/live-mirror benched the donor at the floor for 5min; replicas sat 0 Gn/s and the election had no healthy donor to pick. Fix: stamp only above 50pct of the soft cap (32MB); upload spikes now dip the bufHealth ramp and recover on drain. Smoke-verified via require(): dirty set/clear roundtrip through wsPressure, arm throttle holds, backed-up socket gets 0/100 work picks then rejoins strength-proportional (63/37) on drain, a real 40MB flood still stamps + floors + loses the election to the healthy donor. node --check + require() clean on gpu.js + state.js. ### DONOR v0.3.10 — PRIORITY LANE: THE DROP-CYCLE KILLER (2026-07-12)

SHIPPED (donor-app v0.3.10, donor.rs + Cargo.toml): TWO-LANE WORK QUEUE (Mutex+Condvar, hi drained before lo) — hi lane = deadline-bearing order-insensitive request/reply (ComputeBatch, GpuInit, Upload, Chunk, ChecksumMatrix); lo lane = the fire-and-forget flood (Hebbian, BatchedHebbian, WriteSpike, WriteCurrent, ClearSpike) PLUS Propagate and Readback, which deliberately stay flood-ordered because they READ the spike state the pattern writes ahead of them establish — jumping the queue would hand the curriculum stale reads. Cross-lane reorder of Hebbian vs uploads = the same benign shadow-drift class the auto-resync already re-converges. Hang watchdog composes cleanly (a worker idle in pop() stamps no activity -> no false trip). Expected live effect: batch replies in seconds at any queue depth -> no timeouts -> no kicks -> the ~120MB re-warm churn stops amplifying itself. STILL OPEN: the server-side giant loop pin (98s / 211s, ends exactly at the delayed checkpoint stamp, phase=_teachHebbian, no >2s slice warn) — NOT the drop driver, needs loop-pin instrumentation next.

FIX: pattern-lane shed no longer arms a resync / sets _gpuShadowDirty — the shed (buffer protection) still happens, it is just no longer a false-positive dirty trigger. Only REAL weight-delta drops (TU.25.A hebbian-batch shed) and genuine divergence (donor drop/failover) dirty the weight shadow now, and those clear at the next dream window as intended. node --check PASS, server-only (gpu.js not bundled). ROOT of the silent-chat bug: the deployed brain is server-side; the browser RemoteBrain (remote-brain.js:210) re-emits the server 'response' -> app.js:2336 handler rendered TEXT ONLY, never calling voice.speak(). DECISION (Claude, delegated): browser-side piper (Path B), fully self-hosted, WebGPU->CPU-wasm on the VISITOR's machine. Satisfies every constraint: her exact hfc voice (Equation Unity One V4), no per-response API call (model downloads ONCE at setup, synth is offline+local after), no server GPU (client's GPU is fair game via the WebGPU EP, wasm fallback; our box never crunches it), fully self-hosted (no HuggingFace/CDN), and it never touches the coordinator we just de-froze.

- js/io/voice-piper-worker.js (module worker): text -> phonemes (vendored js/io/vendor/piper-phonemize.js, node builtins aliased to node-empty-stub.cjs for dead ENVIRONMENT_IS_NODE branches) -> onnxruntime-web VITS (executionProviders ['webgpu','wasm'], numThreads=1 so no COOP/COEP) -> 22050Hz PCM. Model OPFS-cached (fetch once). All paths -> /voice-engine/*.
- js/io/voice-piper.js (main-thread courier): preloadVoice(onProgress) / synthPCM(text) / isVoicePreloading(). Spawns /js/voice-piper-worker.bundle.js.
- server/package.json: added build:voiceworker esbuild entry -> js/voice-piper-worker.bundle.js (842KB). Main app.bundle.js stays light — ORT/phonemizer isolated in the worker bundle (verified 0 lib hits in app bundle).
- brain-server.js static MIME: +.wasm=application/wasm, +.onnx/.data=octet-stream (generic ROOT/* handler already serves /voice-engine/* + the worker bundle; verified not gitignored, not rsync-excluded).
- index.html setup modal: #voice-preload progress bar above WAKE. app.js kickVoicePreload() on openSetupModal (gated on #toggle-unity-speech) -> model + worker warm BEFORE wake = zero first-word lag (Gee's ask).
- voice.js: _speakPiper(text) = synthPCM -> perceiveAudio (CDF 9/7) -> reconstructAudio -> _playPcm (equational round-trip, transparent ~38-42dB; graceful fallback to raw piper PCM, then vox-bank, then browser TTS). FIX CANDIDATES: (1) **fire-and-forget Hebbian frames should SHORT-CIRCUIT DROP (not await 30s) when bufferedAmount is over a soft threshold** — CPU CSR is authoritative, the GPU shadow self-heals via the (now-working) auto-resync on drain, so shedding shadow-Hebbian frames under pressure is safe by design; (2) **send-window cap** — bound total in-flight bytes per donor (e.g. 64MB) and pause the batched-Hebbian flush while over it (backpressure-aware flush already half-exists in the batch queue); (3) pace to the WSQ.4 measured linkDownMbps when present.

At 400-900MB buffered and single-digit-MB/s drain, our outbound ping physically cannot REACH the donor for 60-120s → 2 missed pings guaranteed → terminate → reconnect → full re-init + re-upload → deeper flood → next kill. HBGRACE.2 forgives server-loop-block misses but NOT buffer-saturation misses (the +3-forgiven line proves grace works for the wrong cause).   - **ROOT (finally isolated):** the dashboard **Update & Fresh Walk** / **Update & Savestart** buttons already exist and already reach `POST /update` (Gee's click carries a proxy-vouched `X-UAL-User`, so `requireLoopback` admits it). `/update` overlays the new code via `deploy/self-update.sh` correctly — but the SERVICE never restarted, so the box kept running OLD code (the long-standing "button does nothing"). `self-update.sh` is spawned FROM the brain-server process, which runs under systemd `NoNewPrivileges=yes`; a child inherits it and **cannot escalate via sudo even with the `/etc/sudoers.d/unity-brain-restart` grant** → `sudo -n systemctl restart` fails. The WL.4 no-sudo fallback (loopback `POST /restart` → `process.exit` → systemd `Restart=always` revives the overlaid code) is the correct escape, **but its curl sent no `X-UAL-User` header** → on the deployed box (`UAL_PROXY_AUTH=1`) `requireLoopback` 403s it → FATAL, no restart.
  - **[✓ FIX] `deploy/self-update.sh`** — the no-sudo fallback now sends `-H "X-UAL-User: ${DEPLOY_AUTH_USER}"` (new `UAL_DEPLOY_USER`, default `self-update`). `requireLoopback` only checks the header is non-empty, and this is a DIRECT loopback call (nginx not in the path, so nothing strips it) → the vouched identity passes the gate → the box self-restarts into the overlaid code. Comments + the FATAL diagnostic updated to name both traps (NoNewPrivileges-blocks-sudo, header-403). No unit change, no `daemon-reload`, ships in the normal overlay.
  - **Prereqs already satisfied on the box (2026-06-28):** `Restart=always`, server on `127.0.0.1:7525`, deploy key + host key for the `unity` clone. No sudoers rule is even required anymore — the loopback fallback is self-sufficient.

Gee approved close-as-superseded. These were still marked open/in-progress in docs/TODO.md but are resolved or obsolete; moved here verbatim (LAW #0), removed from TODO. The confirmed-root-cause + shipped-fix narrative below is the resolution record.

- [ ] **TU.19 — donor/backpressure error storm + word_motor overflow (Gee-flagged from live dashboard 2026-07-06 ~10:22).** THREE distinct issues, all live on the box RIGHT NOW, all code-fix candidates (NOT benign teach-pin — I mis-triaged them for ~150 passes):
  - **[🚨 ISSUE-A — word_motor_sci CAPACITY OVERFLOW (NEW emission bug, science era)]:** live log `[emit] word_motor_sci capacity overflow — 3272 words exceed frozen band (cellSize=1). Words past index 582 cannot emit; raise word_motor fraction or lower DREAM_WORD_MOTOR_VOCAB_CAP.` The SPEAK.1 frozen bucket geometry for subject=sci froze at `bandSize=582 cellsPerWord=1 maxWords=582` — but science K vocab is 3272 words. **2690 science words physically cannot emit** (index >582 has no motor cells). This is why her science-era emissions lean on the older ELA/persona vocab — the science words literally have no output band. ROOT: `wordBucketCellSizeFor` froze the sci band from `bandSize/DREAM_WORD_MOTOR_VOCAB_CAP` but the sci band (582 cells) ÷ cap gives cellSize=1 with only 582 slots, far below the sci vocab count. FIX candidate: size the frozen band to the SUBJECT's actual vocab count (or raise the word_motor region fraction for multi-thousand-word subjects), not a global cap that starves per-subject bands.
  - **[🚨 ISSUE-B — BACKPRESSURE DROP STORM RETURNED + WORSE, and F5 auto-resync is FEEDING it]:** WS drops 14,715 (11.93/s), ws.bufferedAmount climbing 500MB→1159MB in a continuous sawtooth, GPU buffered 615/500MB, GPU shadow DIRTY, event-loop-lag max **51,002ms**. The TU.17 **F5 auto-resync is making it WORSE, not better**: on each drop it re-uploads `cortex_intraSynapses` (14.2MB) to "resync" — but it fires INTO an already-saturated buffer, stacking multiple 14.2MB uploads (reqId 205105+205106+206217+207319+208178… all intraSynapses, overlapping), which deepens the backpressure → more drops → arms another resync → repeat. Net out total = **301 GB** (10.5 MB/s sustained) = the same 14.2MB matrices re-uploaded thousands of times. The shadow NEVER clears DIRTY because the resync upload itself gets dropped. FIX candidate: (1) F5 must NOT arm a resync while `ws.bufferedAmount` is already over threshold — gate it on a DRAINED buffer; (2) coalesce/dedup in-flight intraSynapses uploads (never >1 pending); (3) the real root — DF.7 re-syncs a FULL 17-matrix+14.2MB replica on EVERY cell-pass, and science K has many rapid short cells (_teachDietClassification, _teachBodyPartFunction, _teachNaturalVsHumanMade… each a checkpoint+resync), so rapid cell-passes = re-upload storm. Throttle DF.7 replica re-sync to a min interval / only on meaningful drift, not every cell-pass.

"GPU shadow DIRTY" is a single flag that conflates THREE independent failure modes we currently can't tell apart: **(1) STALE weights** — donor's uploaded matrices ≠ CPU master because uploads got backpressure-dropped (an I/O problem, ISSUE-B); **(2) WRONG GPU compute** — donor's shader produces a different result than the CPU for the SAME weights+inputs (a shader/precision bug); **(3) WRONG equational math** — the CPU master itself computes garbage (a model bug, e.g. bad CDF 9/7 / Hebbian / cross-projection). PLAN — `scripts/gpu-cpu-parity.mjs` (+ a small server diagnostic hook): (a) connect as a read-only observer; snapshot the CPU master's authoritative sparse matrix (e.g. cortex_intraSynapses) + hash it; (b) read back the donor's resident copy of the SAME matrix + hash → **hash match/mismatch isolates STALE (mode 1) instantly**; (c) if weights match, feed an identical deterministic input vector to BOTH the CPU propagate and the donor GPU propagate, diff the output (maxAbsErr / cosine / first-N divergent indices) → **nonzero diff on matched weights isolates WRONG-GPU-COMPUTE (mode 2)**; (d) run the CPU propagate against a hand-computed tiny reference (known 3×3 sparse case with known answer) → **CPU mismatch isolates WRONG-MATH (mode 3)**. Output: a one-line verdict `STALE | GPU-DIVERGENT | MATH-ERROR | CLEAN` + the numbers. This turns "DIRTY" from a dead flag into a pointed diagnosis, and tells us whether ISSUE-B's re-upload storm is even fixing anything (if it's mode 2/3, re-uploading is pointless). Building this next.

- LOG: `[emit] word_motor_art capacity overflow — band holds 2270 words (2270 cells / 1 per word) but subject has 2548; 277 words past index 2271 CANNOT emit.` She LEARNED 2548 art words but the per-subject emission band only carves 2270 cells → 277 known words have no motor bucket → cannot be emitted. Fix the carve (vocab-aware band sizing) so every learned word gets a bucket — never silence a word she knows.

### ROOT CAUSE (code-read 2026-07-14) + APPROACH A DECIDED (Gee):
- EMISSION runs on the DENSE ~349K language cortex (`cortexCluster`), NOT the 61M sparse main cortex. `word_motor` = top 6% of that cluster (cluster.js:730-731 `wmStart=floor(s*0.940)`, `wmEnd=s`) => ~20,954 cells total at s≈349K.
- Per-subject sub-bands carved by a HARDCODED weight table `WM_DEMAND=[['ela',1.25],['math',0.75],['sci',1.5],['soc',1.2],['art',0.65],['life',0.65]]` (cluster.js:742-755), sum=6.0. Art's slice = 6% × (0.65/6) × 349K ≈ 2270 cells.
- `wordBucketCellSizeFor` (emit.js:917-942) pins cellsPerWord = `max(1, floor(bandSize/50000))` = 1 when bandSize<50K → art holds 2270 words at the MINIMUM packing. Art vocab=2548 → 277 silenced. cellsPerWord can't go below 1 → HARD WALL, not a ratio bug.
- CURRICULUM-WIDE: every subject's vocab is append-only + grows K→PhD (`_ensureWordBucketMap` curriculum.js:11242-11284); full-curriculum emission vocab is tens of thousands of words >> 21K cells. Every band overflows eventually. The 349K language cortex is simply too small to bucket the full vocab.
- SPEAK.1 FROZEN-BAND INVARIANT (emit.js:630-633, 910-916; cluster.js:740-741; curriculum.js:11239-11241): a word's neuron bucket = `word_motor.start + subjBandOffset + bucketIndex×cellsPerWord`; trained `sem_to_word_motor` rows are keyed to those absolute indices. ANY re-carve (moving word_motor.start / sub-band start / cellsPerWord / WM_DEMAND) misaligns every trained weight = the grade-9 word-salad failure. => a hot/savestart re-carve is BANNED; the fix MUST ride a FRESH cluster build (fresh walk) behind a version gate.
- **APPROACH A DECIDED (Gee 2026-07-14):** grow the dense language cortex + vocab-aware per-subject carve, keep the 1-hot bucket design, gate for the next fresh walk (savestarts keep the current walk running untouched until Gee flips it).

## 2026-08-14 — HONEST PROGRESS TELEMETRY (the 85% was a stopwatch, and the frozen spikes were by design)

Gee (verbatim): *"she is at 85% again and its not ticking up anymore.. it was 12-15 secs for each percent upto *5% then it never gets to 86%"* → *"is she fine?"* → *"build #1 and #2 while she does. we can do an update and save start later"*

**WHY THIS EXISTS.** Twice Gee had to ask whether his brain was alive, and both times the answer required reading raw JSON and reasoning about it — once WRONGLY. The instruments were the problem, not the brain.

**WHAT THE 85% ACTUALLY WAS.** `dashboard.html:3434` renders `~N% [time-est] · 0 phases reported · (in progress, server phase counter stuck)` — elapsed-time ÷ expected-duration. It climbs ~1% per ~13s, saturates, and stops. It never measured her at all. `cellPhasesCompleted` only ticks when an OUTERMOST phase FINISHES, and a K cell's first phase runs tens of minutes, so the real counter sat at 0 and the dashboard fell back to a stopwatch.

**WHAT THE FROZEN SPIKES ACTUALLY WERE.** `brain-server.js:4270` — while `cortexCluster._probeGateActive`, the main tick returns EARLY and dispatches no `compute_batch` ("cortex owns GPU exclusively for the probe window"). `totalSpikes` freezing, `gpuHits` sticking, `batchTiming.samples` stopping are all CORRECT during a cell. **I diagnosed this as "her neurons stopped firing" on the previous walk — that was wrong.** The donor drown found alongside it was real and the D.1/D.2 fixes measurably worked (RTT 6,348→816ms, patternSheds 217,015→0, buffer 19.4MB→0, `unhealthy`→false, MB/s 3.87→2.14), but the frozen-spike alarm was a designed pause misread as a freeze.

**AND D.3 WAS BLIND WHERE IT MATTERED.** The watchdog was placed INSIDE `_gpuBatch` — which the tick never calls while paused — so it reported `batchStall: null` while spikes sat frozen. It could not fire in the one situation it was built for.

- **P.1 real progress signal.** `cellPhasesStarted` — outermost phases ENTERED in the current cell, self-resetting on cell-key change, so it moves the instant real work begins instead of after the first phase completes. `vocabProgress` — the live `{label, taught, total, pct, elapsedSec, lastWord}` position inside the running vocab list; the teach loop already computed taught/total for its log line and then discarded it. Held on ONE mutated object (no per-word allocation), updated every word (not every 5th like the event broadcast — the point is that it visibly moves during a long phase), nulled on list completion so a stale position is never reported.
- **P.2 pause-aware stall detection.** Moved out of `_gpuBatch` into `state.js _getProfilingState`, which always runs, and split into two fields that were previously indistinguishable from outside: **`batchPaused`** `{reason, sinceLastBatchMs, cell, expected:true}` for a DESIGNED pause (probe-gate / canonical upload — frozen spikes here are CORRECT), versus **`batchStall`** `{stalledMs, lastOkAt, donorBufferedMB, expected:false}` for a donor connected, nothing paused, and completions stopped anyway — the only state that means something is wrong. The in-`_gpuBatch` copy is now pause-gated too so a designed pause can never train anyone to ignore the alarm.

**VERIFY (no-tests LAW):** `node --check` PASS ×3; ESM `import()` on curriculum (26 exports, `getCurriculumStatus` live); both server mixins load (state 15, gpu 56); all 8 wiring points grepped present; bundle rebuilt KEYLESS (0 live-key hits) carrying `_vocabProgress`.

- **P.5 REAL PROGRESS BARS, NOT TIMERS.** Gee (verbatim): *"io think we also need to make the progress bars real progress bars not timers"*. P.1 published honest data; the dashboard still rendered a stopwatch. `dashboard.html` computed `Math.min(85, round(elapsedMin / EXPECTED_K_CELL_MIN * 85))` — **hard-capped at 85**, which is literally why the bar could never reach 86% and why it saturated and froze on a brain that was teaching normally. It measured wall-clock, never work. Rewired onto the real signals: composite of `cellPhasesStarted` (phases ENTERED) plus the in-flight `vocabProgress` fraction over the expected phase count, capped at 99 so it can never claim done before the cell passes; falls back to `vocabProgress.pct` alone when no phase has registered yet; and keeps the time estimate ONLY as a last resort, now labelled `[time-est — no real signal yet, this is a stopwatch]` so it can never be mistaken for progress again. Scope hazard closed: the sibling `EXPECTED_PHASES_PER_CELL` lives in a DIFFERENT `<script>` block and not at its top level, so it is read through a `typeof` guard with a local fallback instead of throwing ReferenceError. Verified by extracting and parsing every classic inline script block (both OK) and by a LAW grep for task-numbers/operator-name in the public HTML (0).

- **P.6 EXACT PHASE TOTALS, NEVER AN ESTIMATE.** Gee (verbatim): *"wtf is this expected cells per phase or what evr it was? should it be exact # per cell per grade? why are we estimating"*. He was right and the guess was not merely imprecise — it was wrong by **2.25×**: `dashboard.html` hardcoded `EXPECTED_PHASES_PER_CELL = 12` while `runElaKReal` declares **27** `_phaseTick` phases, so the bar rendered 50% at phase 6 when the truth was 22%, from a constant in a public HTML that cannot know which cell is running. FIX: `_cellRunner` now reads the DECLARED count straight from the resolved runner's own source (`Function.prototype.toString` + `_phaseTick(` count) — valid because cell runners are NOT auto-wrapped (the constructor wrap tracks only `_teach*` plus two named probes), so `raw` is the authored function; cached per cell key and logged once. Runners that declare no phases fall back to an OBSERVED total learned from a completed run of that same cell (monotonic, so a restart-truncated cell can't shrink a good count). `cellPhasesTotal` + `cellPhasesTotalSource` are published, and when BOTH are absent the value is **null** and the dashboard shows `phase N (total unknown — first run of this cell)` with **no denominator at all** — a wrong denominator is worse than an absent one.

**NOT URGENT BY DESIGN:** Gee said *"we can do an update and save start later"* — the running walk is deliberately NOT interrupted so V.8 (the grade-wide definition trickle) can finally be observed at her first dream window. These ship on the next Update & SAVESTART.

Donor: `rttMs` **6,348**, `bufferedKB` **19,394** and climbing, `unhealthy: true`. Outbound **11,089 MB in 47 min = 3.87 MB/s**, `msgOut` 74,172 → **153.1 KB AVERAGE MESSAGE**. `patternSheds` +110/sec. Meanwhile the SERVER was healthy: `stepTimeMs` 663, eventLoop p50 21ms, ticks +210/min — the loop span freely with nothing behind it.

**ROOT.** The teach lane ships `write_spike_slice`/`write_current_slice` as JSON arrays of raw integers — 153 KB/message, 3.87 MB/s — into a socket the donor cannot drain. The CHAT.1 lesson (emission went zero-payload / sparse-index binary) was never applied to the TEACH lane. Compounding it: at `SUBSTEPS=24` the donor is busy ~360ms per batch and CANNOT READ ITS SOCKET WHILE COMPUTING, so ~1.4MB piles up per batch.

**OWNED HONESTLY.** Today's two changes moved the bottleneck rather than closing it: Rev's substeps 3→24 made the donor 8× slower to service its socket, and the tick-gap yield fix freed the server loop to push teach frames FASTER. The tick collapse (5,526→663ms) was real, but "running smoothly" was reported without checking `totalSpikes` — the stall was already underway at the time.

**DEPLOY CONSTRAINT honored:** Gee deploys via dashboard buttons only and cannot set env vars on the box, so every fix ships as a **CODE DEFAULT** with the env var retained purely as an override.

- **D.1 pattern-lane flood control** (`gpu.js _donorPatternLaneOpen`): teach-throttle default **20ms → 100ms**, plus **ADAPTIVE back-off** — the interval scales by how far the donor's buffer is past its link cap and by smoothed RTT >1s, bounded ×16 so it can never become an effective mute. A fixed throttle could not know the link was drowning; it kept firing into a full socket while the shed counter absorbed the lie. These frames are per-iteration ephemeral and were already ~100% shed, so pacing them costs nothing real and returns the link to `compute_batch` + hebbian deltas + acks + pings.

- **D.3 silent-stall watchdog** (`gpu.js` + `state.js`): the failure was invisible BY SHAPE — every early return in `_gpuBatch` hands back `null` silently, so "never dispatched" and "healthy idle" are indistinguishable, and the 180s timeout can only fire for batches actually SENT. Now the last SUCCESSFUL completion is stamped (`_lastBatchOkMs`, set only on a real resolve — the timeout path uses the raw resolve so a timing-out donor can never look alive); if a donor is connected and completions stop for >30s it logs a CRITICAL naming buffer/RTT/substeps and surfaces `batchStall` in state. `batchTiming` (the earlier send→reply stopwatch) is now surfaced too — it existed but was never wired into the payload.

## 2026-08-14 — EVERY GRADE LEARNS DEFINITIONS LIKE K (via the dream-trickle, not a 2.2h blocking wall)

Gee (verbatim): *"and why the fuck does it take so long to do kvocab, but every other grade doesnt do a vocab?"* → *"i think option 1 is best,, but i dont want to make k like every other grade... should we instead make every other greade like k"* → *"build it, write the todo fully, and DO NOT FORGET TO BUILD THE TASDK LIST IN THE CLI SO I CAN FOLLOW ALONG ON WHERE U ARE!!! YOU FORGOT TO DO THIS LAST TIME"*

**THE FINDING.** Kindergarten was the ONLY grade running a BLOCKING upfront definition seed. `curriculum.js` fired `_teachWordDefinitions(K_VOCABULARY)` — all 2,247 words × every definition sense — BEFORE a single cell ran. Every other grade got prefetch-ONLY (a fire-and-forget dictionary CACHE warm that binds nothing) with definition binding left lazy. The K block's own comments admitted the upfront Hebbian had been **DROPPED** once for basin-blur risk ("~70k cross-bindings would dense-web the sem region"), called it "BONUS that may be net-negative", and it was later partially re-added at reps 6→2 as "just the seed" — the blocking-at-boot cost was never revisited.

**MEASURED LIVE** (deployed box, build `6fbb992d`): `kVocabTaught` 117 → 143 over 90.3s = **~17 words/min** → K alone = **~2.2 hours** of pre-cell blocking on every fresh walk.

**WHY NOT THE LITERAL "make every grade like K":** the 19 grade vocab files total **49,921 words** (K 2,247 · G1 2,022 · G2 2,083 · G3 1,439 · G4 2,148 · G5 2,030 · G6 2,698 · G7 3,650 · G8 2,914 · G9 4,255 · G10 4,198 · G11 4,171 · G12 4,093 · C1 2,544 · C2 2,037 · C3 1,941 · C4 2,092 · grad 1,786 · phd 1,573). At 17 words/min that is **48.9 hours ≈ 2 DAYS** of blocking pre-cell seed. Gee's instinct (more depth, not less) was right; the PLACEMENT was the problem.

**BUILT — same content, better lane.** The mechanism already existed and was BETTER than K's blocking seed: the dream-trickle binds `_teachWordDefinition(word, {reps: 4, ...})` — **deeper than the blocking seed's reps:1** — with a retry queue for API timeouts and a `_dwOverBudget` window-budget gate. Its only flaw: the queue source was hardcoded to `K_VOCABULARY`, so 18 grades never touched it.

- **V.1 queue generalized** — the K-only lazy init is now a FALLBACK for a boot race / resumed mid-K state; the queue is fed by grade-start enqueues. Field name `_kVocabQueue` deliberately KEPT (it is persisted in saved weights — renaming would orphan every in-flight queue on load).
- **V.2 per-grade enqueue** — each grade enqueues ITS OWN vocabulary at ITS OWN grade start, beside the existing prefetch. Grade-appropriateness is now STRUCTURAL, not filtered: advanced vocabulary cannot be in the queue before its grade begins, so the corpus-bleed rule holds by construction.
- **V.3 K de-blocked** — the blocking upfront pass is skipped; K's 2,247 words route through the same trickle at reps:4. `DREAM_K_UPFRONT_SEED=1` restores the old blocking pass.
- **V.4 drain rate** — `DREAM_TRICKLE_BATCH` 25 → 120, env-tunable. 25 was sized when the queue only ever held K's words. The per-word `_dwOverBudget` check INSIDE the loop is what actually bounds cost (it stops mid-batch when the window's time is spent), so a bigger batch raises the ceiling without lengthening a dream window. **NOT claimed as tuned** — real drain rate must be watched live.
- **V.5 dedup + carry-forward** — `_enqueueDefinitionSeed()` dedups on BOTH axes (already-bound via the persisted `_definitionTaughtWords`, and already-queued) because AoA-ordered grade bands overlap heavily; appends rather than replaces so a prior grade's undrained tail survives; idempotent per grade.

**NET:** ~49.9K words of multi-def Hebbian across the walk instead of 2,247 (**22×**), at reps:4 instead of reps:1-2 (**deeper**), with the ~2.2h pre-cell wall **removed**.

**VERIFY (no-tests LAW):** `node --check` PASS; real ESM `import()` (26 exports) with `_enqueueDefinitionSeed` / `_dreamWindow` / `_teachWordDefinition` / `_teachWordDefinitions` all confirmed on the prototype; all three wiring points grepped present; bundle rebuilt KEYLESS (0 live-key hits) carrying the helper + banner.

**OPEN (V.8, needs Gee's SAVESTART):** confirm the walk reaches its first cell in seconds rather than ~2.2h, and that `💤 dream trickle: N words processed … N words remaining in the definition-seed queue (grades enqueued: …)` lines show the queue actually draining across grades. If it lags, raise `DREAM_TRICKLE_BATCH`.

## 2026-08-14 — TOLERABLE / REV PR #3 MERGED (substeps 3 → 24 at biological scale — the GPU idles 98.5% of every tick)

Gee (verbatim): *"Rev made another PR, same thing update local and both repos"*

github PR #3 — *"The GPU is idle 98.5% of every tick — measured on the live brain"* — head `8cab418`, 1 commit, 1 file, **+36/−1**, conflict-free. Fetched via `refs/pull/3/head` → local `pr3/head`, merged `--no-ff` into `feature/merge-rev-pr3-substeps-0814` off main, cascaded develop → main, pushed to BOTH remotes. Authorship preserved (`Reverend Dr Tolerant`).

**THE ONE SUBSTANTIVE LINE:** `_SUBSTEPS_AUTO` at the `>1,000,000` neuron tier, **3 → 24**. Sub-1M tiers deliberately UNCHANGED (never measured against them).

**HIS MEASUREMENT (live deployed brain, 306M neurons, one RTX 4070 Ti SUPER):** `stepTimeMs 3010.5` (one tick takes three seconds) · `ticks/sec 0.728` · `cpuPercent 6` (CPU idle) · `eventLoopLagMs 4` (loop NOT starved) · `gpuMisses 0` (donor answers every batch) · donor self-reported `20.3 Gneurons/sec`. Arithmetic: 7 clusters × 3 substeps × 306M = 919M neuron-steps/tick, which at 20.3 Gn/s is **45ms of real GPU math inside a 3010ms tick — the GPU works 1.5% of the time**. The other ~2965ms is round-trip (dispatch, per-cluster readback, ack handling, state broadcast) and is **FIXED PER TICK regardless of substeps**.

**WHY THE OLD LADDER WAS BACKWARDS:** it LOWERED substeps as the brain grew (10 → 5 → 3) on the assumption that more neurons mean more per-substep cost to throttle. But the throttle only ever shrank the payload, never the overhead — so at biological scale it maximised the fraction of wall-clock spent on protocol. The bigger the brain, the MORE substeps should ride per round-trip, because the round-trip is the expensive part. 24 substeps ≈ 360ms of GPU math per ~3300ms tick: **8× the brain steps for ~10% more wall clock**. Deliberately not pushed to the ~60 the arithmetic allows, because `compute_batch` has a real timeout and a donor stalling mid-batch trips the zombie-kick path.

**THIS IS THE FIRST OF REV'S PRs THAT CHANGES DEPLOYED BEHAVIOUR BY DEFAULT** (PR #1 landed on the browser-only brain; PR #2's attention relay is opt-in). Watch after deploy: `compute_batch` timeouts, donor disconnects mid-batch, dashboard responsiveness. **ROLLBACK IS ONE ENV VAR — `DREAM_SUBSTEPS=3`** (the knob PR #2 added, which is what makes this safe to try).

**NO FRESH WALK, NO BUNDLE.** No weight-format or geometry change → Update & SAVESTART. `server/brain-server.js` is server-side CommonJS and not in the esbuild entry graph, so no browser bundle rebuild. `brain-server.js` IS in `BRAIN_CODE_FILES` so the code hash moves; `DREAM_KEEP_STATE=1` (Savestart) bypasses the hash check and weights survive. VERIFY: `node --check server/brain-server.js` PASS; diff confirmed to be the single `_SUBSTEPS_AUTO` constant plus its rationale comment.

## 2026-08-15 — donor-v0.3.14: DEVICE-SIDE PATTERN SCATTER — the walk was ~28× slower, not the promised ~3×; the donor's dense-host-vector habit was the wall

Gee (verbatim): *"hows our girl? shes been at it for 12 hours... are we sure everything is good? 12 hrs and only phase 2/25 of the first cell?"* → *"if option 1 will fix it do it"*

**THE MEASURED PROBLEM (build `20f3b856`, 12.6h uptime):** teaching CORRECT but ~104 teach/min vs ~2,970/min unpaced = ~28× slower. 12.5h inside `_teachLanguageMechanics` at `phaseWork 4/14` → ~39h for ONE phase, ~3 days for ONE cell. Collateral: 12.6h inside one phase = ZERO dream windows = no consolidation, no vocab trickle. The donor was eating ~5MB/s sustained (25GB in 84 min) at ~10 pattern groups/sec absorbed.

**THE ROOT — read out of `cuda.rs`, and it overturned the "coalescer" framing:** every teach op materialized a DENSE host vector spanning the full region/matrix and blocking-copied it over PCIe on the single worker thread: `write_spike_slice`/`write_current_slice`/`clear_spike_region` = full region (~360KB each for a 90K-row band); `hebbian` = TWO full-matrix vectors (pre over cols + post over rows — **6MB each on the 1.5M-row cortex intra matrix, per plasticity frame**). The v0.3.13 binary frames fixed the PARSE cost; the EXECUTION of each frame still paid megabytes of host alloc + synchronous PCIe for a few hundred sparse indices.

**THE FIX — donor-v0.3.14, device-side scatter:** four new CUDA kernels (`fill_zero_u32` / `fill_zero_f32` / `scatter_ones_u32` / `scatter_vals_f32`) + `cuda.rs` rewired so all five ops (`write_spike_slice`, `clear_spike_region`, `write_current_slice`, `hebbian`, `propagate`) upload ONLY the sparse index list (~KB) and zero+scatter in-place on the GPU. Everything rides the ONE default stream → clear→write→plasticity ordering is preserved by stream order with ZERO host synchronization on the teach path (propagate keeps its readback sync — it returns data). Per-op host cost drops from ~milliseconds of alloc+copy to ~microseconds of launch calls; the worker thread drains the socket instead of grinding memcpys. Protocol UNCHANGED — same SPRS 7/8/9 + type-3 frames, zero server edits; the version bump announces itself via `appVersion`.

**PTX REALITY (recorded for the next editor):** regenerated with the real nvcc on this box (CUDA 13.0 — Gee's machine hosts the donor GPU). nvcc 13 dropped `compute_60` → built `-arch=compute_75` (PTX ISA 9.0, needs r580+ driver). Cards below Turing or on old drivers hit the EXISTING loud module-load-failure path and fall back to wgpu — never silently compute zero. The deployed donor is cc 8.9 on a CUDA-13-era driver. Host-compiler note: VS 18 needed `-allow-unsupported-compiler` (device-only compile — host compiler only preprocesses). Regen command updated in the .cu header.

**VERIFY (no-tests LAW, stronger than v0.3.13's):** the kernels are REAL-COMPILED — nvcc built the shipping kernels.ptx, 8/8 `.visible .entry` points verified (4 original + 4 new). Rust: full read-back of every edited region; positional arg walk against each kernel signature; borrow walk (all-immutable reborrows; `get_mut`/`slice_mut` eliminated from the write paths); stream-order walk; buffer-lifetime walk (cudarc stream-ordered frees land after the consuming kernel). Dead host-side scatter helpers removed. No cargo locally — OUR Forgejo CI compiles on the tag, same flow as v0.3.13.

**SCOPE (honest):** wgpu-backend donors (AMD/Intel, and any NVIDIA that falls back) keep the dense-write path — their `queue.write_buffer` is staging-belt async and they are not the deployed donor; a WGSL scatter port is future work if a wgpu donor ever hosts the walk. Browser donors unchanged (JSON, BT.5 scope-cut).

No donor-side execution change can beat the pipe. **The structure that saves us:** ~20 msgs/s against ~1.4 teach calls/s = ~14 near-identical frames per call — rep loops (reps 2–50) re-ship byte-identical payloads.

**BUILT — three legs, one release:**
- **(a) REPEAT-FRAME PROTOCOL (the speed lever).** New SPRS type 12: when a teach payload for (type, name) is byte-identical to the last one SENT on this socket, a ~30-byte repeat frame ships instead and the donor re-executes its cached copy — exact same GPU result, ~10–50× fewer bytes on the traffic that dominates. Server: per-SOCKET `Buffer.equals` cache in all three pattern senders (types 7/8; 9 is header-only) + `gpuSparseHebbian` (type 3, equality on the body since the header carries a fresh reqId; the repeat rides a real reqId and acks as type 3 so the await contract is identical). Cache discipline: update ONLY on a confirmed send (`_donorPatternSendGated` boolean for 7/8; a <64MB buffered-amount gate for 3 — far below any drop path — with delete-on-uncertainty), keyed per socket on BOTH ends so a reconnect starts in lockstep. Version-gated ≥0.3.15 (TU.20.12 pattern — negotiation, not a fallback), one-shot log at selection.
- **(b) RESIDENT BOUND-HEBBIAN (the type-5 stub killed).** The native donor's type-5 batched-hebbian handler acked and applied NOTHING since v0.3.11 — every bound-projection GPU shadow discarded. Now: chunk flags-bit-2 binding metadata is CAPTURED (frames.rs `Binding`), stored per matrix on BOTH backends, and each (name, lr) op launches plasticity reading the bound clusters' RESIDENT spike buffers at the bound offsets (kernels already take srcOffset/dstOffset — zero new kernels, kernels.ptx untouched). Engine AFFINITY in MultiEngine: a bound matrix routes to its clusters' GPU; clusters on different GPUs → binding dropped LOUDLY (standalone). Bounds-guarded: an ill-fitting window skips (counted, never OOB). compute.html semantics exactly.
- **(c) PER-TYPE TEACH TELEMETRY.** `wsPressure.teachOutByType` (frames + bytes per SPRS type) + `teachOutBytesSaved` + `repeatTeach` — the river's composition is READ off the state payload now, never again inferred from average message sizes.

**VERIFY (the WC.4b lesson applied):** `cargo check` PASSES both feature sets LOCALLY (cuda 1.5s, full default 36s — rustup installed this session); `node --check` gpu.js + state.js PASS; repeat-frame + binding-block byte-walks MATCH both codecs (alignment walked field by field); cache-discipline walk done; state.js full-file read before edit (1,438 lines).

## THE GUIDING PRINCIPLE

**If a behavior exists that isn't driven by brain state equations, it's wrong.**

Every piece of Unity's output must trace back to:
- **Cortex prediction** (ŝ = W·x + b) — what she expects
- **Amygdala valence/arousal** (V(s) = Σw·x, energy-basin attractor) — how she feels about it
- **Basal ganglia motor selection** (softmax over learned channels) — what action she takes
- **Hippocampus recall** (Hopfield attractor + persona sentence memory) — what she remembers
- **Cerebellum error correction** (ε = target − output) — what she fixes
- **Hypothalamus drives** (homeostatic gradients) — what she needs
- **Mystery module Ψ** (√(1/n) × N³) — her consciousness level
- **Oscillation coherence** (Kuramoto) — her focus/scatter
- **Language cortex** (semantic n-grams over learned embeddings + T14 tick-driven motor emission) — her words

Nothing else. If it's not in that list, it's an appendage, and it gets ripped out.

## OPEN TASKS — 2026-08-14 · HONEST PROGRESS TELEMETRY (stop making Gee interpret frozen counters)

> Gee (verbatim): *"she is at 85% again and its not ticking up anymore.. it was 12-15 secs for each percent upto *5% then it never gets to 86%"*
> Gee (verbatim): *"is she fine?"*
> Gee (verbatim): *"build #1 and #2 while she does. we can do an update and save start later"*

**WHY THIS EXISTS.** Twice now Gee has had to ask whether his brain is alive, and twice the answer required me reading raw JSON and reasoning about it — once WRONGLY. The instruments are the problem, not the brain.

**WHAT WE LEARNED (2026-08-14, build `98383ea6`):**
- The **85% is a TIME ESTIMATE, not progress.** `dashboard.html:3434` renders `~N% [time-est] · 0 phases reported · (in progress, server phase counter stuck)` — elapsed-time ÷ expected-duration. It climbs ~1%/13s then saturates. It never measured her.
- **Frozen `totalSpikes` / `gpuHits` is BY DESIGN.** `brain-server.js:4270` — while `cortexCluster._probeGateActive`, the main tick returns early and dispatches NO `compute_batch` ("cortex owns GPU exclusively"). Spikes freezing during a cell is EXPECTED.
- **I misdiagnosed this as "her neurons stopped firing"** on the previous walk. The donor drown found alongside it was real and the D.1/D.2 fixes worked (RTT 6,348→816, sheds 217,015→0, buffer 19.4MB→0, unhealthy→false) — but the frozen-spike alarm was a designed pause misread as a freeze.
- **D.3's watchdog is blind in the exact case it exists for:** it lives INSIDE `_gpuBatch`, which is never called during the probe-gate pause, so it reported `batchStall: null` while spikes sat frozen.
- She IS progressing: `cellSubPhases` +48/sec, WORD-INT ~1.1s/word, donor clean.

### TASKS

- [x] **P.1** REAL progress signal — surface honest per-cell progress so "is she moving?" is answerable by LOOKING: phases STARTED (not just completed — the first phase is long and `cellPhasesCompleted` sits at 0 for tens of minutes), the active phase name, and the live vocab-list position (`_vocabIdx`/`_vocabTotal`, which the teach loop already computes and then throws away after logging)
- [x] **P.2** PAUSE-AWARE stall detection — move the check OUT of `_gpuBatch` (which isn't called while paused) into the state builder that always runs, and split the two states that currently look identical: `batchPaused {reason, ms}` for a DESIGNED pause (probe-gate / canonical upload) vs `batchStall {...}` for a genuinely unexplained stop. A designed pause must never read as a stall, and a real stall must never read as null
- [x] **P.5** REAL PROGRESS BARS, NOT TIMERS — Gee (verbatim): *"io think we also need to make the progress bars real progress bars not timers"*. Every other grade (`curriculum.js:8735`) gets prefetch-ONLY: a fire-and-forget dictionary cache warm that never blocks, with definition binding left lazy. The K block's own comment says the upfront Hebbian was **DROPPED** for basin-blur risk ("~70k cross-bindings would dense-web the sem region"), calls it "BONUS that may be net-negative", then it was partially re-added at reps 6→2 as "just the seed" — and the blocking-at-boot cost was never revisited.

**MEASURED LIVE (2026-08-14, deployed box, build 6fbb992d):** `kVocabTaught` 117 → 143 over 90.3s = **~17 words/min**. K alone = **2.2 hours** of pre-cell blocking on every fresh walk.

**WHY NOT THE LITERAL "make every grade like K":** the 19 grade vocab files total **49,921 words** (K 2,247 · G1 2,022 · G2 2,083 · G3 1,439 · G4 2,148 · G5 2,030 · G6 2,698 · G7 3,650 · G8 2,914 · G9 4,255 · G10 4,198 · G11 4,171 · G12 4,093 · C1 2,544 · C2 2,037 · C3 1,941 · C4 2,092 · grad 1,786 · phd 1,573). Feed every grade's vocab into that queue AT ITS OWN GRADE START and she gets 49,921 words of multi-def Hebbian (22× today's 2,247), deeper (reps 4 vs 2), with ZERO blocking — and no corpus bleed, because enqueue-at-grade-start means PhD words can never surface at K.

## OPEN TASKS — 2026-08-14 · PHASE-LATCH: the outermost-phase flag corrupts permanently on the FIRST concurrent teach

> Gee (verbatim): *"is this right? 50k events and still phase 1, 0% complete?"*
>
> Gee (verbatim, mid-batch correction): *"fallback? you should know we cxode it right the first time which means fallbacks are illegal"*
>
> Gee (verbatim, mid-batch correction): *"no the names shall never not be there.. wtf are you talking about!!! code it cortrectly"*
>
> Gee's dashboard paste (verbatim):
> ```
> phase: _teachLateralInhibition (+0.1s)
> current cell progress
> 0% · phase 1/25 · 0 complete · _teachAntiHebbian (+0s) · 29.2 min
> course / grade / phases / cells / events
> Foundational Reading / pre-K / 0 / 0 / 45.2k
> ```

**ANSWER: NO. It is not right, and it is not a display bug — the phase ledger is dead.**

**THE PROOF, read off Gee's own paste (no inference).** The cell-progress line names `_teachAntiHebbian` with `+0s` elapsed. `_teachAntiHebbian` is a PRIMITIVE — `curriculum.js:11974` / `:14090` call it from inside `_teachAssociationPairs` / `_teachQABinding`. `getCurriculumStatus` only publishes a primitive there via the `exact:false` fallback at `curriculum.js:3089`, which fires **only when `cluster._outermostPhase` is null**. The same line carries **no `work N/N` tail**, which means `phaseWork` is null, which means `_phaseWorkTotal` is 0. `_outermostPhase` and `_phaseWorkTotal` are assigned in the SAME block — `curriculum.js:2683-2688`, `if (isOutermost && cl)`. Both absent ⇒ **`isOutermost` has not been true once this cell.**

**THE MECHANISM — a latch, not a glitch.** The constructor auto-wrap decides outermost by `const prev = cl._activePhase; const isOutermost = prev === null;` and restores `cl._activePhase = prev` in `finally` (`curriculum.js:2641/2660/2789`). That save/restore is only sound if teach calls never interleave. **They do:**
- `server/brain-server.js:2256` — `this.curriculum._teachWordDefinition(word, {label:'CHAT-DEF'}).catch(...)` — fire-and-forget from chat, and it awaits a **network** dictionary fetch (`timeoutMs` up to 20000).
- `server/brain-server/chat.js:246` — `this.curriculum._teachAssociationPairs(pairs, {...})` un-awaited from the chat path.
- `server/brain-server/chat.js:599` — `await curric._teachAssociationPairs(...)` from curiosity-followup.
- `js/brain/curriculum.js:13620` — `this._teachWordDefinition(word, {label:'EMIT-DEF'})` un-awaited on emission.

Interleave: walk phase **P** enters (`prev=null`, outermost ✓, `_activePhase=P`) → chat's **D** enters mid-await (`prev=P`, nested) → **P finishes first** and restores `_activePhase = null` → **D finishes second** and restores `_activePhase = P`, a phase object that already exited. From that instant `_activePhase` is permanently non-null, so **every subsequent phase in the entire walk sees `prev !== null` and is misclassified as nested — forever, brain-wide, until restart.** One chat message or one `EMIT-DEF` is enough to poison the rest of the run.

**WHAT IT ACTUALLY BREAKS (this is the part that is not cosmetic):**
1. `passedPhases` never appended by the auto-wrap → `cellPhasesCompleted` frozen at 0 → **`0 complete` after 29.2 min is the ledger, not her pace.**
2. Resume-skip is dead — `⤳ PHASE SKIPPED` can never fire, so **every restart re-teaches from scratch**.
3. `cellPhasesStarted` degrades to `passedPhases + 1` = the constant `1`. **`phase 1/25` is a stuck counter, not her position.**
4. `phaseWork` null → the honest within-phase bar shipped this morning can never move → **`0%`.**
5. `_cellPhaseObserved` never learns a cell's real phase count.
6. `server/brain-server/gpu.js:2641` idle-detection reads `!_cc2._activePhase` and will now never see idle.

**WHAT IS NOT BROKEN:** the teaching itself. Nested calls always execute — only the skip/persist path is outermost-gated. Those **45.2k events are real Hebbian work**; her weights are moving. It is the ledger that is lying, in the direction of under-reporting.

### THE WORK

- [x] **L.1** **DONE.** Replace the save/restore-across-await with a latch-proof in-flight STACK. `cl._phaseStack` of per-call tokens; `isOutermost = stack.length === 0` at entry; on exit remove **by identity** (`splice(indexOf(token),1)`) and set `_activePhase = stack[stack.length-1] || null`. Self-healing: once every in-flight call exits the stack is empty and the next walk phase is outermost again. No dead phase object can ever be resurrected.
- [x] **L.2** **DONE.** Guard persist/skip against foreign teach calls. With a stack, a chat-driven `_teachWordDefinition` firing while the walk is BETWEEN phases would qualify as outermost and get written into `passedPhases` as a phase of the current cell — which would then be SKIPPED when the runner legitimately reaches it. Fix: persist/skip only when the method name is one the current cell's runner actually declares. `_cellRunner` already computes that name set at `curriculum.js:7044-7050` and throws it away after taking `.size` — keep it as `this._cellPhaseNames[cellKey]` and gate on it. Visibility/telemetry stays on for every call; only the LEDGER is gated.
- [x] **L.3** **DONE.** Make the fallback honest about itself. When `outermostPhase.exact === false` the dashboard currently renders the primitive name as if it were the phase. Label it so a latch (or any future gap) is visible on screen instead of masquerading as progress.
- [x] **L.4** **DONE.** Verify — no-tests LAW: `node --check`, ESM `import()` (catches dup bindings `--check` misses), bundle rebuild, and re-read the edited regions.
- [x] **L.5** **DONE.** Docs + FINALIZED migration, atomic commit, cascade develop→main, push BOTH remotes.
- [x] **L.7** **DONE.** *"fallback? you should know we cxode it right the first time which means fallbacks are illegal"* + *"no the names shall never not be there.. wtf are you talking about!!! code it cortrectly"* - every fallback branch deleted, including ones written earlier the same day: the `exact:false` publish-the-primitive branch; `_persistedPhaseTotalFor()` (method removed) and the `declared || observed || persisted` cascade; the in-memory observed-total learner; `cellPhasesTotalSource` + `cellPhasesPersisted`; and in `html/dashboard.html` the WHOLE post-render override block (cell progress was computed in two places that could disagree) with its five-branch cascade ending in `Math.min(85, elapsed/EXPECTED_K_CELL_MIN * 85)`, plus both heuristic constants. `_declaredPhaseNames()` always returns the set - proven by deriving it for 48 cells (6 subjects x 8 grades, pre-K through PhD): every one non-zero, so there is nothing to fall back to.
- [>] **L.6** **MERGED into LIVE-VERIFY (combined) at the bottom of this file.** ⏳ LIVE-VERIFY on Gee's next Update/Fresh-walk: cell-progress line must name a REAL phase (`_teachLetterCaseBinding`-class, not `_teachAntiHebbian`) with a **minutes-scale** `+Ns`, must carry a `work N/N` tail that climbs, and `0 complete` must leave 0 when phase 1 lands.

## OPEN TASKS — 2026-08-14 · THE COMPUTE LAYER IS BUILT ON FALLBACKS — teaching must be GPU-ONLY

> Gee (verbatim): *"why does it keep training when i disconnect the doner? that should NOT be possible!!!, RIGHT?"*
>
> Gee (verbatim): *"find out how it is even doing that to find the issue? its like its using the server cpu or something weird"*
>
> Gee (verbatim): *"fallback!?!?!?!?!!??!?!?!"*
>
> Gee (verbatim): *"fallbacks!!!!?????"*
>
> Gee's decision (verbatim option chosen): **"Walk stops, she stays awake"** — *"curriculum walk HALTED (no CPU Hebbian, ever); brain tick / propagate running (CPU); chat / voice she can still talk; dashboard 'PAUSED - no compute substrate'; DONOR BACK: walk resumes instantly"*

**ANSWER: he is right, and his guess was right — it IS the server CPU.**

**THE FINDING.** The GPU was never required anywhere. It is an accelerator layered over a CPU implementation that is always present, selected per call:

- **Hebbian — `js/brain/cluster/hebbian.js:169`.** The GPU branch runs and `continue`s. When `_gpuProxyReady` is false execution **falls through** to lines 262–296 and runs the FULL CPU Oja over millions of destination rows (`_sparsePool.hebbianUpdate` or `_ojaUpdateChunked`). Same math, same weights, on the box's Xeon.
- **Propagation — `js/brain/cluster.js:3296`.** `const useGpu = this._gpuProxyReady && this._cachedCrossCurrents;` then line 3308 *"CPU fallback — GPU cache miss or GPU proxy not ready yet"* → `proj.propagate(srcSpikes)`.
- The code announces it in its own logs: **`PARTIAL — falling back to CPU for failed matrices`** (`hebbian.js:683`), and `hebbian.js:282` records the all-night **`"2/17 uploaded, 15 fell to CPU"`** loop.

**AND THE GATE I SHIPPED THIS MORNING WAS ITSELF WRONG.** `_awaitComputeSubstrate` (`curriculum.js:10888`) tests `brain._gpuClient.readyState === 1` — *is a socket open*. The compute path tests `cluster._gpuProxyReady` — *did the weight upload finish*. **Two different questions.** A donor connected-but-not-uploaded passes the gate and still lands on the CPU branch. On top of that the gate has a **120s grace** and is sampled **every 64th** nested teach call, and `DREAM_NO_DONOR_GRIND=1` re-enables grinding on purpose. That is a timer discouraging a fallback, not an architecture forbidding one.

**THE CORRECT ARCHITECTURE.** Compute substrate is a **deployment property decided once**, not a per-call `if`. The server's biological-scale brain REQUIRES the GPU substrate: no substrate → the walk halts, and no teach math runs at all. The browser/standalone brain (6.7K neurons, no donor ever) has the CPU implementation as its ONE path. One decision, made at construction, never re-decided per call — so there is no branch to silently take.

## OPEN TASKS — 2026-08-14 · PER-SUBJECT GRADE COLUMN SHOWS THE LAST GRADE PASSED, NOT THE ONE SHE IS IN

> Gee (verbatim): *"sure, lets make sure its all correct, but we will do update savestart later on that issue and we will walk current build till we get to a good spot after the live-verify"*

**THE ISSUE (caught on the live dashboard while ELA-K was mid-cell).** The per-subject table read `Foundational Reading / pre-K / 1 / 0 / 24.8k` while the card header directly above it read `Kindergarten (Common Core K.RF / K.W / K.L / K.SL / K.RL …)`. Both were rendered from the same status payload, disagreeing about which grade she is in.

**ROOT — the column is the LAST-PASSED pointer, not the live one.** `getCurriculumStatus` overrides the per-subject grade with `cluster.grades[sub]` (`curriculum.js:3015`), and `cluster.grades[subject]` is assigned **only inside `if (result && result.pass)`** (`curriculum.js:8721`) — i.e. when a cell COMPLETES. It is seeded `{ela:'pre-K', math:'pre-K', …}`, so mid-K it still reads `pre-K`. `courseNameFor(sub, grade)` is computed from that same stale value, so it inherits the staleness. **Correction to my first reading of this:** the course name did NOT look wrong in the caught case — `courseNameFor('ela', …)` returns `Foundational Reading` for pre-K, kindergarten AND grade1, so the string matched by coincidence. It would show the previous grade's class at any boundary where the name actually changes (e.g. math grade8→grade9 `Algebra I`, science→`Biology`). Verified by calling `courseNameFor` directly rather than assuming.

**Also note:** the seeded default makes "passed pre-K" and "has passed nothing at all" indistinguishable in that field — both read `pre-K`. Any correct derivation has to consult `passedCells`, not the pointer.

**THE CORRECT DERIVATION — one rule, both cases.** The grade a subject is AT = the first grade in `GRADE_ORDER` whose cell is not in `cluster.passedCells`. For the subject currently being taught this yields exactly the in-flight grade; for idle subjects it yields the grade they will run next. Terminal case (every grade passed) yields the last grade in the order. No branch on "is this the active subject", no second source to disagree with the first.

### THE WORK

- [x] **GC.1** **DONE.** Derive the live per-subject grade from `passedCells` + `GRADE_ORDER` and use it for BOTH the grade column and `courseNameFor()`, replacing the `cluster.grades[sub]` override.

## 2026-08-15 · PS.5 DECIDED — **NO wiring change.** The sparsity is deliberate lamination; the defect is elsewhere.

> Gee (verbatim): *"live verify and decide on Ps.5"*

### LIVE VERIFY (build `64c71147`, the deployed one)

- **She PASSED `ela/kindergarten`.** Now on **`math/kindergarten`, phase 22/24, 21 complete**, 91.6 min in.
- **569 teach/min**, `sinceLastTeachMs` 0 — actively teaching. The liveness telemetry is doing its job.
- **`kVocabTaught` climbed 2 → 22** across 3 consolidation passes. The TB trickle-first fix is working on the deployed build; the PS.2 empty-queue fix (not yet deployed, `definitionQueue: None` confirms) should take it much further.

### THE DECISION: do NOT raise cross-projection density. Evidence:

1. **`initTopographicProjection` already guarantees `fanout = Math.max(1, round(density × cols))`** — every row it is *permitted* to touch gets at least one entry. There is no density shortfall.
2. **The zero-entry rows are LAYER-MASKED, by design.** `cluster.js` builds `dstMaskAB = buildLayerMask(bRegion, 2)` — **L4 only** — and `initTopographicProjection` writes `rowPtr[i+1] = rowPtr[i]` for any row failing the mask. That is Felleman & Van Essen 1991 hierarchical connectivity: cross-projections terminate on L4 stellate input cells. Raising density would fight the lamination the K-microstructure work deliberately installed, and cost VRAM to do it.
3. My earlier framing ("a quarter of her word buckets can never learn") was **wrong today and wrong about the cause.** The ELA band is 18,750 rows for 1,977 words = **9.5 rows per bucket**, so every bucket currently contains live rows and emission works. Corrected here rather than left standing.

### THE ACTUAL DEFECT — bucket carving ignores lamination

`_teachWordEmissionDirect` carves each word's bucket as a raw contiguous range: `bStart = bandStart + wi * bucketSize`. `grep -c layerId js/brain/curriculum/kindergarten.js` = **0** — the carving has no idea which rows can receive input. So a bucket may be composed largely, or entirely, of rows that no projection terminates on.

**Why it is not hurting her now, and why it becomes fatal:** at ~9.5 rows/bucket a bucket almost always contains some L4 rows. At the stated **~60,000-word K→PhD target against 90,000 word_motor rows, `bucketSize` collapses to 1** (`Math.max(1, floor(90000/60000))`) — and then a word whose single row is not L4 **can never be emitted, no matter how long she trains.** The failure arrives gradually as vocabulary grows, which is exactly when it would be hardest to attribute.

- [x] **PS.6** **CLOSED SUPERSEDED — PS.6-as-filed failed the 60k-word target (only ~22,500 L4 rows); the shipped fix is the word_motor lamination exemption (OI.5a), verified structurally on the live walk (sem_to_word_motor 89,961/90,000 rows recruited).** Carve word buckets from PROJECTION-RECEIVING rows. `_ensureWordBucketMap` / `wordBucketCellSizeFor` must draw each word's bucket from the L4 rows of its sub-band (the rows `sem_to_word_motor` actually terminates on) instead of raw contiguous ranges. Costs zero VRAM and respects the lamination instead of fighting it. **Requires a word-bucket-map VERSION BUMP** — changing the geometry re-points every already-trained word→bucket association, so it must take effect on a FRESH WALK, never silently mid-run.

At base 100ms the ceiling was 1,600ms of braking; dropping base to 15ms silently dropped the ceiling to **240ms** — not enough to hold a bursting lane, so the buffer runs to the cap, sheds, stales the group, suppresses the Hebbian. Two further defects: braking engages only ABOVE 4MB (too late relative to a 16MB cliff), and `_patternLaneWait`'s copy of the law lacks the RTT term (the two governors can disagree).

**FIX — one steep early control law, identical at both sites:** `mult = clamp((buf / 2MB)², 1, 133)` plus the existing RTT term. At 2MB → 15ms; 4MB → 60ms; 8MB → 960ms; ≥11MB → ~2s ceiling. Brakes rise with the SQUARE of pressure and reach full force well before the cliff, so sheds (and therefore stales/suppressions) become the rare true-saturation case. Empty lane still runs at 15ms — the healthy-link throughput the LB change was for.

**THE FIX SHAPE:** implement type-5 batched-hebbian FOR REAL on the native donor — cluster-BOUND matrices whose plasticity reads resident spike state (written by the type-7/8/9 pattern frames) at the bound src/dst offsets. Gee (verbatim, the fork answer): *"Do it correctly so that it fucking runs fast and we get our 1500 teach/ min back...!!!!"* · Gee (verbatim): *"no cutting shit"*

**Target:** `_teachHebbian` 3.8s/call at 12M (88ms at 1.5M — 43×), pair phases at ~25 teach/min vs the 1300–1500 band. Cause: the intra matrix (360M nnz) was the ONE matrix with no GPU dispatch (T18.18 removed its OOM-prone full-array shadow) — pure CPU, per pair, per rep.

**The read COLLAPSED the design:** the donor's `init_cluster` is fully generic (any name/regions), `hebbian_bound` resolves clusters by name with offset windows and tolerates late residency, and t9/t11 handlers look regions up generically — **NO segment tables, NO new kernels, NO donor release: the 0.3.17 binary already does everything.** The build is SERVER-ONLY:
- **Pseudo-cluster:** `_gpuInitLangPseudoCluster()` gpu_inits `langCortex` (langCortexSize, top-level standalone regions, tonic/noise 0; never in compute_batch — written solely by teach frames; ~96MB donor VRAM), fired before the canonical upload; gated on the donor speaking template spikes (≥0.3.17).
- **Intra binding:** initGpu uploads `cortex_intraSynapses` WITH binding src=dst=`langCortex[0..size]` (server mode only); `intraSynapses` added to the CSR-free whitelist so checkpoints NEVER lose the CPU arrays.
- **Teach-frame TWINS:** t11 spike templates + t9 clears also land on `langCortex/<region>` (identical region-relative payloads — the pseudo regions ARE the standalone absolute spans; ~300–600B each).
- **Dispatch:** `intraSynapsesHebbian`/`AntiHebbian` fire `hebbianBound('cortex_intraSynapses', ±lr)` EVERY call — full training mass on the substrate, ~30B/op through the SAME stale-guarded type-5 lane as every cross-projection — gated on an IDENTITY CHECK (`pre===post===lastSpikes`; custom-vector callers like `_teachHebbianAsymmetric` stay CPU) + the pseudo-init flag. **CELLBOUND.H - the deferral cursor, PERSISTED.** CELLBOUND.A stopped a runaway phase on a clean rep boundary and reported its remainder, but nothing REMEMBERED it: the next visit re-entered at full authored reps and paid for the landed reps twice - the same unbounded multiplication one level up, across ~114 visits. `cluster._phaseRepCursor` banks reps STILL OWED under `<phaseName>::<teachLabel>` (keyed on the phase NAME, deliberately not the cell key, because the whole point is resuming on the NEXT cell's visit). On arrival the owed count replaces the authored dose (clamped, never above it, never below 1 - one full presentation always lands, same law as the `rep > 0` guarantee); on a clean finish or a convergence early-exit the debt is paid and the key is deleted.
