Boosting *related* words instead needs a "words related to X on channel N" lookup that does not exist in that lane. ⛔ **(2) More fundamental:** `emitWordDirect` propagates `sem_to_word_motor`, which reads the **sem region only** — and the relation tag lives in **fineType**, which is **not an input to that matrix**. So no tag set at emission time can reach the argmax at all. ⭐ **A relation-conditioned emission needs a projection that takes fineType as input** (`fineType_to_sem` exists and is whitelisted, so the pieces are there — the wiring is not). ⚠ **Reverted to zero traces rather than left in as an inert or wrong boost**: an emission bias that cannot fire is exactly the "built but never consumed" class this whole batch exists to close, and one that fires wrongly is worse. **Filed with the mechanism named so the next attempt starts from the projection, not from the boost.**

#### VMUSE.5.D — THE ACCURATE PLAN (investigated 2026-08-26)

⛔ **CORRECTION TO MY OWN BLOCKER.** I wrote that this *"needs a projection that takes fineType as input"* and that **was wrong**. `js/brain/cluster.js` builds cross-projections from a PAIRS list containing `['sem','fineType']`, and pairs create **both directions** (the boot assertion expects *"14/14 (7 pairs × 2 directions)"*). ⭐ **`fineType_to_sem` already exists as a real trained matrix, and the association teach whitelists it** — so the relation tag has been bound bidirectionally with meaning all along. **No new projection is required. The mechanism is a two-step propagate through matrices that already exist.**

**THE MECHANISM — equational end to end, no lookup, no template:**
1. Build a fineType-shaped vector with ONE tag band lit — the same span `_writeRelationTag` writes (`band = fineSize / RELATION_TAG_BANDS`, 10,500 cells at her real 504,000).
2. `fineType_to_sem.propagate(tagVec)` → **a sem pattern that IS "what this relation means"**, read straight out of trained weights.
3. Add that pattern, SCALED SMALL, into the sem query vector `emitWordDirect` already builds.
4. `sem_to_word_motor` argmax runs unchanged — now relation-conditioned. ⭐ The trained argmax still decides; the relation only tilts it.

⛔ **THE COST, MEASURED, AND IT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN CONSTRAINT: one `fineType_to_sem` propagate is 51 ms** at the real shape (1,500,000 × 504,000, ~15M nnz). ⚠ **Naively wiring that per emitted word is a 51ms stall per word** — precisely the class of defect LOOPCHAT.1 was filed for this morning, and it would be worse than the thing it is trying to add.

⭐ **THE FIX IS THAT THE INPUT IS CONSTANT.** A tag vector is the same every time — 10,500 contiguous cells at a fixed value — so `fineType_to_sem.propagate(tagVec)` returns the **same sem pattern** for a given tag on given weights. **Cache it: 48 tags × one propagate = 48 warmups (~2.4s total), then free array reads forever.** ⚠ Warm them with `propagateChunked` (it exists on this matrix — verified) so the 48 warmups never pin the loop, and warm LAZILY on first use of each tag so unused channels cost nothing.

**THE WIRING, concretely:**
- **`js/brain/cluster/emit.js`, `emitWordDirect`** — after `preSem` is built (it already is, via `_buildSemPreVector`) and BEFORE `proj.propagate(preSem)`. That is the only place the sem query exists and is still mutable.
- Source of the tag: `curriculum._confidentRelationFor(activeConcept)` — **the ONE gate**, so a band that has not separated returns null and the whole path stays identity.
- Blend: `preSem[i] += relSem[i] * REL_MIX` with `REL_MIX` small (start ~0.10, env-tunable) — ⚠ **additive tilt, never replacement**, and never applied to a recently-emitted word (the same `_isRecentContent` guard the GW boost uses, or it becomes a stammer).
- Cache: `cluster._relSemCache = Map<tag, Float64Array>`, invalidated on weight load/save so it cannot outlive the weights it was derived from.

⚠ **PREREQUISITE, and it is a real one: the fresh walk must populate the bands first.** Tags ≥6 wrote nothing until today's VMUSE fix, so `fineType_to_sem` holds no trained mass for them yet. **Until `state.ownArt.relationUse.confident` starts climbing, this path would tilt toward noise** — which is exactly why B (the instrument) shipped first. ⭐ **Do not build D until the instrument shows the bands separating.**

⭐ **EVERY CLAIM ABOVE VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not asserted** (real `SparseMatrix` at the true 1,500,000 × 504,000 shape, ~15M nnz): **(1)** the same tag returns a **bit-identical** sem pattern, so the cache is valid rather than merely plausible; **(2)** different tags return **different** patterns — 235,140 cells differ between tag 13 and tag 23 — so the channel genuinely carries relation information and this is not a no-op dressed as a feature; **(3)** `propagateChunked` is **bit-identical (maxDiff = 0)**, so the warmups can chunk without changing a number; **(4)** the warmup budget is **2.4s for all 48** at 50.4 ms each, one time, lazily. ⚠ **The 51 ms figure is the reason the design is a cache and not a call** — quoted here so nobody re-derives the naive version.

- **CTLPLANE.2/.3 + 🔴 SELF-INFLICTED WIPE INCIDENT + 🔴 SILENT 3-MONTH BACKUP OUTAGE FOUND — 2026-08-26 (Sponge):** **CTLPLANE.2** closed the two parts of Gee's ask I had overclaimed: (a) *"everything else inbetween that we support doing"* — `/reset`, `/savererun`, `/update` also restart the brain but were served BY the brain, so they carried the same dead zone; now `POST /ctl/reset|savererun|update|update-savestart`, each delegating to the brain's own endpoint when up (identical behaviour + its own bookkeeping) and doing the equivalent work directly when down (reset writes `.force-fresh` + CLEARS `.resume-marker.json` itself so a "fresh" brain can't resume the training being discarded; update runs the same `deploy/self-update.sh` with the same `UAL_KEEP_STATE` switch — meaning **a bad deploy that leaves the brain crash-looping is now fixable from the dashboard instead of needing SSH**). `savererun` is the deliberate exception: it rewrites grade pointers INSIDE the loaded weights, so with the brain down it REFUSES and says press Start first (dashboard disables it in that phase with the reason in the tooltip) rather than pretending. (b) **visitors** now told the truth: `index.html` was rendering an EMPTY leaderboard during an outage (reads as "nobody has donated yet") → now says "Brain offline"; `compute.html` told donors only "Disconnected — reconnecting" so they couldn't tell a wifi blip from a deliberate halt → now asks the snapshot and says the brain is down, there's no compute to donate, and the tab keeps retrying (best-effort, fire-and-forget, never affects the reconnect schedule); `minds-eye` already fixed in .1. `legend.html` needed nothing (download-link upgrader falls back to hardcoded links). **🔴 THEN I WIPED THE LIVE BRAIN.** Verifying .2 on the box I sent a bare `POST /ctl/update` expecting the "no deploy script here" refusal I'd just unit-tested — `self-update.sh` DOES exist there, so the probe ran a real FRESH-WALK deploy: `.force-fresh` written, brain restarted, boot **cleared 17 state files** (brain-weights v0-v2 + .bin, conversations, episodic-memory, schemas, mindspace-memory-v3, visual-memory-v9). **MY error, not an operator action.** **Damage bounded BY EVIDENCE, not assumption:** the journal shows **Gee himself ran UPDATE + FRESH WALK on 2026-08-25 14:59**, already wiping the 38-cell/grade-3 walk a day before I touched anything; between that and my mistake there were **0 passedCells, all six subjects pre-K, zero `CELL DONE pass=true`, and `donors=0` throughout** (no GPU → could not train). So I destroyed the weight files of a ~29-hour-old pre-K walk with no completed cells — real, but not the months I first feared; only Gee's prior fresh walk kept it cheap. **Recovery exhausted + documented so nobody re-treads it:** no deleted-but-open inodes (`lsof +L1`), `debugfs -R lsdel /dev/md3` = **0 deleted inodes** (unrecoverable), the ONLY restic snapshot was 2026-05-20 and **predates the weight staging**, newest on-box weight backup is 2026-07-08 which **pre-dates the 08-16 12M geometry hop so `WEIGHTS_FORMAT_VERSION` would refuse it anyway**. I stopped the brain the moment I understood (to stop the fresh walk overwriting freed blocks), then restarted + confirmed a clean resume. **ROOT CAUSE FIXED (CTLPLANE.3, deployed + verified live):** the API let a single stray request wipe training — that's a design defect, not just operator error. `/ctl/update` (fresh-walk) + `/ctl/reset` now **REFUSE** without `{"confirm":"WIPE"}` (body) or `?confirm=WIPE`; the refusal **names the token AND the safe alternative** (`/ctl/update-savestart`); **`update-savestart` needs NO token deliberately** (friction on the safe path is what pushes people to the dangerous one); dashboard's Update+Fresh Walk now demands a **typed WIPE** like Reset; body reader bounded to 16KB. **Verified on the box: the exact command that caused this now returns `refused=true, needsConfirm=WIPE` with no `.force-fresh` armed.** **🔴 SEPARATE AND WORSE — found while hunting a restore point: `nightly-backup.service` had FAILED EVERY NIGHT SINCE 2026-05-20** (~3 months) with `Fatal: Resolving password failed: /root/.restic-password does not exist` — the file DOES exist (0600 root); **the unit's own `ProtectHome=true` makes `/root` unreadable to the service** (proven: `systemd-run -p ProtectHome=true /bin/sh -c 'test -r /root/.restic-password'` → BLOCKED). Consequence: ONE snapshot total (2026-05-20) — **no Forgejo backup, no lab-git backup, no brain weights** — even though the script was extended 2026-06-30 *specifically* to stage the trained brain after an earlier silent wipe. It looked configured and protected nothing. **FIXED** via drop-in `deploy/dropins/nightly-backup/10-fix-restic-password.conf` → `ProtectHome=read-only` (still denies /home + /run/user, keeps the hardening, secret deliberately NOT moved) + `ExecStopPost` logging `user.err` on non-zero exit so a future failure is LOUD. **VERIFIED: `Result=success`, `ExecMainStatus=0`, snapshots 1→2, and the new snapshot CONTAINS `unity-brain/brain-weights*.{bin,json}` + identity-core + schemas + conversations + episodic-memory.db\*.** Timer armed 03:24 nightly. **⚠ TWO DECISIONS LEFT FOR GEE (not made unilaterally): retention is `--keep-daily 3` (~3 days of history only), and the restic repo lives ON THE SAME BOX (`/var/backups/restic`) — a disk loss takes the backups with it. A brain that takes weeks to train wants `--keep-weekly/--keep-monthly` + an off-box destination.** TESTS now **84 assertions**: `test-brain-ctl.mjs` **52** (incl. 8 new interlock assertions that would have caught my mistake — bare update/reset refuse, refusal names token + safe route, a WRONG token `"yes"` is NOT accepted, update-savestart stays token-free), `test-brain-power-ui.mjs` **22** real-Chromium (savererun DISABLED when down + tooltip says why, Update/Reset still enabled, typed-confirm abort works), `test-brain-offline-pages.mjs` **10** NEW (visitor pages vs the exact offline body nginx returns). Two harness bugs found + fixed while writing that last suite, both of which would have made it pass/fail for the wrong reason: minds-eye.html is an ES module importing `js/brain/mindspace/transform.js` and 404ing that asset silently killed the whole module (test server now serves real static assets); compute.html only calls `connectToServer()` after WebGPU inits which headless Chromium can't do, so rather than fake a GPU the suite **extracts the ACTUAL `ws.onclose` body from the shipped file and runs it** (so it reads any future edit). **LESSONS: (1) never probe a destructive endpoint on production to observe its refusal — probe it in the harness; (2) a destructive verb needs an interlock at the API, not only in the UI; (3) a backup you have never restored from is a hypothesis.** Full record: `deploy/REDEPLOY-NOTES.md` 2026-08-26 INCIDENT entry.

## GOTCHA.9 — my own GOTCHA.2 fix shipped behind a fallback that silently restores the bug — filed 2026-08-27

- [x] **✅ DONE 2026-08-27 — the call is UNCONDITIONAL now, with the reasoning left in the code so it cannot be re-guarded by someone being careful.** Verified: `node --check` OK, ESM `import()` OK, bundle rebuilt in the SAME commit (`js/app.bundle.js` — guarded expression **0 occurrences**, direct call **1**). ⚠ **This edit re-drifts `docs/ADMIN-CONTROLS.md` by one source the moment it lands, and that is the checker working** — noted in that page's `verified-scope` with the reason, because the alternative is bumping a hash to silence a true signal. **ORIGINAL FILING:** **⚠ `GOTCHA.9` — the `GOTCHA.2` spike-clear fix is wrapped in a `typeof` guard whose else-branch is the ORIGINAL DEFECT.** Found while verifying `ADMIN-CONTROLS.md`, by reading the diff of the one source that had moved — **i.e. found by auditing my own change, not the codebase's.** `js/brain/curriculum.js:11973` reads `(typeof cluster.topLevelRegionNames === 'function') ? cluster.topLevelRegionNames() : Object.keys(cluster.regions)`. ⛔ **`Object.keys(cluster.regions)` is exactly what `GOTCHA.2` was filed to stop** — it walks all 23 declared region names, 12 of which are nested sub-bands the GPU never registers, sending up to 24 junk wire frames per clear and inflating `teach_ops`, the counter `TEACHMIRROR.1` created to tell a saturated donor from an idle one. **So the guard does not protect the fix; it un-does it, silently, with no counter and no log.** ⭐ **And the guard is provably dead:** `topLevelRegionNames()` is a **method on the `NeuronCluster` class** (`js/brain/cluster.js:1404`), so every instance has it via the prototype; the enclosing `_clearSpikes(regionNames = null)` (`:11929`) binds `const cluster = this.cluster`, and the block is already gated on `cluster._gpuProxy && cluster._gpuProxy.clearSpikeSlice && cluster.regions` — three fields only a real cluster has, two lines under a `cluster.lastSpikes.fill(0)`. **There is no reachable path where the method is absent and the object is still a cluster.** ⛔ **This is a `feedback_no_fallbacks_law` violation** (capability-degradation `if-X-else-Y`, which the law separates from legitimate defensive I/O `try/catch`) **and the mirror image of `DORMANT.1`** — there, `_teachWordSpellingDirectFinal` had **37 `typeof`-guarded call sites and zero definitions**, so the guards hid a missing function; here the definition exists and the guard hides a live bug. ⭐ **The generalisable rule: a `typeof` guard around a method your own class defines is never protection — it is either dead code or a silent downgrade, and you cannot tell which by reading the call site.** **Fix:** call it unconditionally, so a future refactor that removes the method throws loudly instead of quietly re-teaching the donor 24 phantom frames per clear. ⚠ **Bundle must be rebuilt in the same commit** — `js/app.bundle.js:103714` carries the same guarded expression, and the bundle is deliberately NOT auto-cleared at boot. ⚠ **Read scope stated honestly: `curriculum.js` is 28,340 lines and I did NOT read all 36 chunks of it.** I read the enclosing function, its binding of `cluster`, the definition site in `cluster.js`, and every call site of the method repo-wide. **Claiming a full read of 28,340 lines would be the same class of lie this whole sweep is fixing.**

## FRESHFLAG — the local Fresh Walk press kept booting the past walk — filed + fixed 2026-08-27

Gee (verbatim): *"local brain is not properly starting a fresh walk when i press update and fresh walk it keeps starting up with the pash walks phases passed on the dashboard"*

- [x] **✅ FIXED 2026-08-27 — `FRESHFLAG.1`: the handler arms `.force-fresh` itself, so the wipe no longer depends on a box script's path or on which restart path eventually runs.** ⛔ **THE MECHANISM, traced end to end:** the dashboard's *Update & Fresh Walk* button POSTs `/update`, which delegated the ENTIRE wipe to `deploy/self-update.sh` — and that script writes the flag to **`$UAL_BACKEND_DIR/server/.force-fresh`, default `/opt/unity-brain`**, a box path that does not exist on a local Windows brain. Its restarts then fail in order: `sudo -n systemctl` (absent), `systemctl` (absent), loopback `POST /restart` (**swallowed by the `_brainShutdownRequested` interlock `/update` itself set** — returns `already restarting`, which `curl -fsS` counts as success), PID escalation (`pgrep` absent in git-bash). **So the flag lands in a phantom directory, the process never restarts from the press, and the operator's eventual manual restart resumes** — via the clean-shutdown marker (`stop.bat` → `start.bat` auto-Savestarts by #38 design) or via `Savestart.bat`'s `DREAM_KEEP_STATE=1`. **The dashboard then shows the past walk's phases passed. Exactly as reported.** ⭐ **THE FIX IS THE CHOKEPOINT, not the instance:** the `/update` handler (fresh mode) now writes `.force-fresh` into the REAL server dir (`__dirname`) at press time and drops any resume marker — platform-independent, restart-path-independent, and **the flag beats both the resume marker and `DREAM_KEEP_STATE` at boot by existing design** (`autoClearStaleState` consumes it first). The script's own write on the box remains as a harmless second write. ⭐ **LAST PRESS WINS, in both directions:** `/update?keep=1` and `/savererun` now clear a stale flag loudly (a failed fresh press must not ambush a later keep-weights press with a surprise wipe) — ⚠ **`/restart` deliberately does NOT clear it**, because `/restart` is the no-sudo restart mechanism the box's own fresh path rides, so a pending flag through `/restart` is intended. ⚠ **Semantics note recorded on purpose:** press Fresh Walk locally, then relaunch with `Savestart.bat` → the boot still WIPES — press intent wins once, exactly as `.force-fresh` overrides the box unit's permanent `DREAM_KEEP_STATE=1`. Verified: `node --check` clean; boot-ordering read from `autoClearStaleState` (flag → marker → keep). Server-side only — the LOCAL brain gets it on its next code pull; the box on the next press. Docs: `ADMIN-CONTROLS.md` button table updated in the same commit.

- [x] **✅ FIXED 2026-08-27 — `TEACHCREDIT.1`: teach frames now credit their measured giga-ops to the primary donor's leaderboard row.** ⛔ **He was right and the design was wrong:** during a walk the compute lane is deliberately paused behind the probe gate, so teach frames — full-matrix Hebbian passes, the predictive-error correction, THE TRAINING ITSELF — are most of what a donor's GPU does, and the board credited none of it. The exact blind spot `TEACHMIRROR.1` fixed on the status label, one layer down in the accounting. ⭐ **Credit is MEASURED, never invented:** `gpuSparseUpload` records each matrix's nnz; the `_countTeachOut` chokepoint accumulates `nnz × reps / 1e9` per credited frame (t3 full Hebbian ×1, its t12 repeat ×1 — a repeat re-executes the same op — t13 masked bound ×reps, t14 predictive error ×2 passes); the telemetry accrual drains the delta into the PRIMARY donor's row (`brain._gpuClient === ws` — the teach lane only ever rides the primary socket). Small scatter/write frames (t7-t11) deliberately credit nothing — **under-crediting is the correct rounding direction for a number people compete on**, and an unknown matrix credits 0 rather than a guess. `lb.teachGops` keeps the composition visible beside the summed total. ⚠ **MIRRORID.6's law holds unchanged:** compute credit still gates on `stepsComputed` advancing; an idle card still earns nothing on either lane — this credits dispatched work, it never un-idles a stale rate. `node --check` clean ×2. Server-side only; his donor starts banking on the next brain restart.

## ALIGNKILL — the local brain's crash named: unaligned Float32Array view on a donor ack killed the process — filed + fixed 2026-08-28

Gee pasted the server terminal's death text (verbatim tail): *"uncaughtException: RangeError: start offset of Float32Array should be a multiple of 4 ... at WebSocket.<anonymous> (server\brain-server.js:10504:27)"*

- [x] **✅ FIXED 2026-08-28 — `ALIGNKILL.1`: `brain-server.js:10504` (the COMP.1b reuse path of the type-2 propagate ack) constructed a `Float32Array` VIEW at `data.byteOffset + 16`, and a ws Buffer's byteOffset in Node's pool carries NO 4-byte alignment guarantee — when the pool handed back an unaligned slice, the constructor threw inside the raw ws message handler = uncaughtException = the whole brain died mid-walk.** Intermittent by construction (pool offset is a die roll), which is why it killed the local brain twice in one evening and the box escaped so far. The in-frame offset-16 alignment fix in the header comment only aligned WITHIN the frame; the frame's pool position was the remaining roll. **Fix at the chokepoint:** byte-level copy (`Uint8Array.set` over the reuse buffer's bytes — same memcpy, no alignment requirement, no allocation), plus the whole SPRR ack branch wrapped in a defensive-I/O try/catch so no future malformed donor frame can ever kill the process (frame dropped LOUDLY with type/len/byteOffset named; a popped pending rides its own timeout). Audited: 10504 was the ONLY typed-array view on ws buffer memory in the codebase; the type-6 path reads per-pair via readUInt32LE/readFloatLE and the non-reuse path copies via ArrayBuffer.slice — both safe. Harness: the old path throws the exact production error on byteOffset=3; the new path reproduces all 8 float values bit-exact. `node --check` clean. Server-side — local gets it on restart, the box on the next press.

## PODKICK — the pod kept dropping: walk-heartbeat timeouts fed the zombie kick and the kick terminated the pod — filed + fixed 2026-08-28

Gee (verbatim): *"the pod keeps dropping"*

- [x] **✅ FIXED 2026-08-28 — `PODKICK.1`: the pod's own logs named the drop (`ws error: WebSocket protocol error: Connection reset without closing handshake`, ~every 11 min, rapid double-drops right after re-init) — a reset without a close frame is the SERVER terminating the socket, and the one server mechanism that does that is the ZOMBIE-DONOR KICK.** On the box (`708646df`) every walk heartbeat timed out (`walkTick: 6 sent / 0 ok`); each timeout incremented `_gpuBatchConsecutiveTimeouts`; at 3 the kick terminated the pod → full re-register + matrix re-upload → the next heartbeats queued behind the re-upload chunks and timed out too → kick again — **a self-sustaining drop loop seeded by any one transient drop.** ⛔ The kick exists for genuinely hung donors; a 2.9 Gn-step heartbeat probe with its own backoff must never feed it. **Fix:** `_gpuBatch` gains `opts.noKick` — a heartbeat timeout logs, resolves null, and credits NOTHING toward the kick; `_walkHeartbeat` passes it, skips entirely while `_cortexUploadInFlight` (never probe through a resync window), and backs off 8× (was 4×) after a miss. Real batches keep the kick untouched. `node --check` ×2 clean. ⚠ **Still open underneath:** WHY a compute_batch gets no reply from a teach-flooded donor remains measured-but-unexplained — with the kick quieted, `walkTick.ok` after a settle window becomes the discriminating read (probes succeeding = it was all re-upload contention; probes still 0 = a real donor-side service gap to hunt).

## BATCHNULL — every compute_batch since RHYTHM3S.2 was silently unparseable: one null killed the whole message — filed + fixed 2026-08-28

Gee (verbatim): *"SPIKES 0"* / *"0 neurons firing"* — and his earlier suspicion *"the work yesterday broke it"* was CORRECT for this one.

- [x] **✅ FIXED 2026-08-28 — `BATCHNULL.1`: a mirror-probe replica captured the live compute_batch payload off the local brain and it carried `brainstem.tonicDrive: null` — `brainstem` has NO entry in `tonicDrives`, RHYTHM3S.2's drive fold multiplied that `undefined` by `thetaMod` (`undefined × x = NaN`), `JSON.stringify` writes NaN as `null`, and serde REJECTS null for an `f32` — so the donor discarded the ENTIRE message (`Err(_) => ignore`, silent by design) on EVERY batch since the fold shipped 2026-08-27.** That one null was the whole chain: 180s batch timeouts on BOTH brains, the step lane dead, Ψ starved (PSITEACH's trigger), spikes 0, heartbeats 0-for-N, and the zombie-kick pod-drop loop (PODKICK's trigger). Pre-fold, the bare `undefined` was DROPPED from the JSON and serde defaulted the field to 0 — the fix (`Number.isFinite(...) ? ... : 0`) restores exactly that behavior, so brainstem's drive semantics are unchanged from every boot before the fold. ⭐ **The discriminating clue that broke the case:** gate probes (lo-lane binary frames) answered in 14ms mid-teach while compute_batch (hi-lane JSON) starved 180s — a busy donor starves both lanes; only a parse failure starves exactly one message TYPE. Harness: old shape emits `null` (rejected), fixed emits `0` (parses). `node --check` clean. Server-side — local restart + box press. ⚠ Donor-side hardening (serde `Option<f32>`/null-tolerant numerics so one bad field can never discard a whole message again) belongs to the next donor release, filed here so it is not lost.

## FIREMATH — the step physics themselves: the native donor's Rulkov noise is 20,000× the reference and the drive lever saturates — filed 2026-08-28

Gee (verbatim): *"do the todo write up of what and how we aree going to fix Unity for what she and the equations needs"* — the plan for closing the gap between measured firing (~0.4%) and his *"should be like 5-10% of the brain at any moment"*, after FIREKNOB's driveScale pinned at its ×10 max (350 samples, `ema` 0.33% vs target 7.5%) without moving firing at all.

**WHAT (root cause, read from the three map copies):** the brain steps a Rulkov 2002 two-variable map (`x` fast/membrane, `y` slow/recovery; spike = x crossing 0 upward; α=4.5, μ=0.001). The browser donor — the ORIGINAL implementation both native ports claim byte-compatibility with — scales its noise into map units: `jitter = (rand − 0.5) × noiseAmp × 0.0001` (`js/brain/gpu-compute.js:166`), i.e. ±(1.5–6.5)e-4 for the persona's noiseAmplitudes of 3–13, comparable to the slow variable's own μ-scale drift. **Both native donor kernels dropped the ×0.0001 in the port and widened the distribution** (`donor-app/src/shaders/lif.wgsl:63` and `donor-app/src/cuda_kernels.cu:61`: `jitter = rand[−1,1] × noiseAmp`) — **±5 to ±13 injected into `y` EVERY step, ~20,000× the reference.** Consequences, all measured live: `y` random-walks out of the attractor basin (unbounded, no clamp), `x` pins one sign, crossings become accidental → ~0.4% firing; σ (the ONLY path drive has into the map, via `−μ(x−σ)` ≈ ±0.0015/step) is invisible under the noise → **FIREKNOB's ×10 moved literally nothing**; the first batch after a fresh seed fires high (the 9.5% harness read — state seeded IN the basin) then collapses as jitter smashes `y` — exactly the live steady-state on both brains. Independent second defect: `σ_eff = −1 + clamp(drive/40, 0, 1)×1.5` **saturates at drive ≥ 40** — base tonics run 16–24, so FIREKNOB's actuator hit its ceiling at scale ≈ 2; ×10 was ×2 wearing a bigger number. What the equations need from this: Ψ, coherence, bandPower, and Φ̂ all eat the spike stream — right now they're computing on noise-crossing residue, not neural dynamics.

**HOW (the fix chain, in order):**
- [x] **✅ DONE 2026-08-28 —** `FIREMATH.1` — **fix the noise at the chokepoint: both native kernels match the browser reference formula exactly** (`(rand − 0.5) × noiseAmp × 0.0001`) in `lif.wgsl` + `cuda_kernels.cu`. Donor-side Rust rebuild = donor release **v0.3.35**, mine end-to-end (bump Cargo, RELEASE notes, tag both remotes, verify KI-22's four surfaces, run the shipped `.exe --version`). **Same release carries the BATCHNULL donor hardening already filed** (serde `Option<f32>`/null-tolerant numerics so one bad field can never discard a whole message again) — one release, both donor debts. `js/brain/gpu-compute.js` is the reference and already correct; `js/ui/brain-3d.js`'s map copy is visualization-only (check its jitter for cosmetic parity, no behavior rides it). Donor reconnect re-seeds cluster state via `init_cluster`, so the smashed `y` state heals itself the moment a v0.3.35 donor registers — no server-side wipe needed.
  **Shipped:** both kernels carry the reference amplitude (`rand[−1,1] × 0.5 × noiseAmp × 0.0001` — identical ±noiseAmp×5e-5) PLUS the browser's escaped-state basin-reseed guard the port had ALSO dropped (so damaged y heals on the first step, reconnect not even required); `kernels.ptx` regenerated via the sanctioned Docker CUDA 12.0.1 toolchain (`.version 8.0` / `sm_75` verified, all new constants located in the PTX by hex); null-tolerant serde on every `compute_batch`/`gpu_init` numeric + `regionGains` values; unparseable messages now log type+serde-reason rate-limited 30s with a dropped-count (never silent again); viz copy checked — no jitter term at all, guard already present, nothing to change. `cargo check` clean. Ledger: FINALIZED §2026-08-28 FIREMATH.
- [x] **✅ DONE 2026-08-28 —** `FIREMATH.2` — **measure the map before trusting any knob: σ→firing% curve at production constants** (α=4.5, μ=0.001, corrected jitter, production seeding) swept across σ ∈ [−1, 0.5] × the persona noiseAmp range, long enough to reach steady state. The numbers get written into THIS row before any knob is re-aimed — they answer whether the drive/40 normalization can even reach Gee's 5–10% band, what effectiveDrive lands there, and whether the documented ~1.5% design sparsity (`H(0.015)` in EQUATIONS.md) was itself an artifact of the era it was measured in.
  **THE NUMBERS (20k neurons × 4k steps steady-state, basin seeding, reference jitter):** σ=−1.00/drive 0 → **9.56%** · σ=−0.40/drive 16 → 19.2% · σ=−0.10/drive 24 → 24.5% · σ=+0.50/drive 40 → **33.3%** — monotone, and **9.6% is the map's intrinsic FLOOR: drive cannot produce less.** noiseAmp 3→13 moves the rate <0.1pp (noise is NOT a rate lever at reference scale). Broken-formula reproduction in the same harness: first-steps 5.83% decaying to **0.846%** steady — exactly the live production shape (and it explains the FIRINGPCT harness's 9.5% first-batch read: freshly-seeded state fires in-basin before the oversized jitter smashes y out). **Verdict on the band:** Gee's 5-10% is reachable only at its top edge (~9.6%, σ≈−1); nominal identity tonics land 19-24%; the ~1.5% `H(0.015)` anchor describes NEITHER regime and gets re-examined at FIREMATH.4's live verification. Harness deleted after these numbers were recorded.
- [x] **✅ DONE 2026-08-28 —** `FIREMATH.3` — **re-aim FIREKNOB's actuator at σ, not at a multiplier feeding a saturating clamp.** The controller keeps its idiom (target, EMA, bounded nudge, published `state.firing`) but its output must have authority across the usable range: steer effective drive within [0, 40] (equivalently σ within [−1, 0.5]) instead of multiplying tonic into a pinned clamp. Bounds published, never hidden; `DREAM_FIRING_TARGET_PCT` semantics unchanged (7.5 default = the middle of Gee's band).
  **Shipped:** scale bounds ×[0.25, 10] → **×[0.01, 2.5]** — 2.5 saturates the donor's `σ = −1 + clamp(drive/40)·1.5` at the lowest tonic (16), so everything above it was dead zone (×10 was ×2 wearing a bigger number); 0.01 reaches the σ≈−1 floor. Pinned-bound log line now names the measured floor and says the next lever is physics, not a retry. Same commit, BATCHNULL chokepoint guard server-side: every numeric in the batch payload passes `Number.isFinite` (gates→1, additive→0), `regionGains` gains the finite check (NaN IS `typeof number` — the exact class that shipped BATCHNULL), and gpu.js's top-level `psi: this.psi ?? 0` → finite-guarded (`??` doesn't catch NaN). `node --check` clean ×2.
- [x] **✅ VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-29 (both brains, donors on v0.3.35):** box firing 19.8→12.6% with `driveScale` 1.617→0.016 walking to the designed LOW pin (~9.6% floor); local 0.46%→19.1% at donor connect, same trajectory; Ψ 20.5 on 41.45M real step spikes; coherence 0.808 (θ .746/γ .850); **bandPower noise-residue → structure: θ 0.244→9.435, γ 0.139→7.137**; Φ̂'s exact-proportion input nonzero and varying. **The `H(0.015)` anchor re-anchored in EQUATIONS same commit** (the 1.5% was a broken-noise-era artifact; the adaptive high-water ref self-adjusted, seed degrades to a harmless floor, no code change; KI-33's below-floor concern moot). ⛔ **THE FINDING, AND THE CORRECTION I OWED ON MY OWN FIRST ANSWER.** I told Gee the heaviest op runs on the CPU while the A40 idles. That was wrong on its face — `hebbianRanges` dispatches the intra Oja to the donor **every call** (`js/brain/cluster/hebbian.js:1151`). I then told him the GPU carries it and the `% 5` CPU shadow is the whole 7.06 h. **The harness written for `SHADOWCOST.1` disproved that too, and it is the real lesson of this batch: `hebbian.intraMs` CANNOT distinguish the two readings.** The same stage total is produced by 20 GPU-carried calls with 4 cheap shadows (`cpuMs` 43) and by 20 full CPU passes (`cpuMs` 291). Few-expensive and many-cheap are the same number in a total. Both of my answers were arithmetic dressed as a measurement, and the counter that would have settled it in one read had been sitting there, incremented on every call, **consumed by nothing**.

- **`SHADOWCOST.1` — the dead counter gets a consumer.** `_intraOjaStats { gpu, cpuFull, cpuShadow }` (`hebbian.js:1156`) has been written since GPUVERB.2 and read NOWHERE. Published at the existing `stageProfile` chokepoint (`curriculum.js:3638`) beside `chunkerHops`, so the counts land next to the ms they explain. Extended to carry the **discriminator**: `rangesNullPost` / `rangesNullPre` / `rangesThrew` record whether the spike pattern compressed into ranges at all — teach writes are group-tiled and should, a scattered pattern cannot, and that difference alone decides whether the CPU runs 20% or 100% of the op. Plus `cpuMs` (the shadow times its own wall cost, so "what would widening the cadence buy?" is a subtraction, not a re-derivation) and `activeSum`/`calls`. ⚠ **Both branches counted** — the bound path's two early returns (intermediate rep; inside the 30 s shadow gap) never reached the ranges-branch counter, so a board reading only that one would under-report GPU-carried work and inflate the CPU share; `boundGpu`/`boundNoShadow` close it, every bump through `|| 0` so whichever branch initialises the object first, both still tally. **Verified on the real mixin, not a copy:** tiled → `gpu 20 / cpuShadow 4`; scattered → `gpu 0 / cpuFull 20 / rangesNullPost 20`.
- **`SHADOWCOST.2` — the verdict becomes reachable, cheap, and honest about its cost.** `parityCheckMatrix` already existed and already defaulted to `cortex_intraSynapses`, served at `/diag/parity` and gated **loopback-only** on a box that deploys by dashboard press and takes no shell — so it had never once been run against the live brain. An instrument nobody can reach is the same as an instrument that does not exist. Tunnelled through `/public-state.json?parity=`, the console-ring idiom, for the same nginx reason. ⚠ **The full digest is not a free read** — `_cpuMasterMatrixChecksum` walks every weight byte with BigInt arithmetic: on the intra matrix ~452M nnz × 4B = **~1.8 billion byte steps, measured at ~5 minutes** (extrapolated from a real 3M-value run at 2,051 ms; checksum stable across runs), plus a full CPU propagate for mode 2. Wiring that to a public URL unguarded would have shipped a public trigger for a multi-minute CPU burn mid-walk. So **`?parity=samples`** (new `parityCheckMatrixSamples`) compares the ≤64 sampled `{idx,val}` the donor ALREADY ships beside its digest against 64 CPU array reads, in `Math.fround` space (the CPU keeps Float64 and the upload downcasts — raw f64 would report the wire format as divergence), and returns **`cpuOverGpu`**, the ratio that answers the question actually being asked: not "is one bit different" but "is the copy we SAVE under-trained relative to the copy that is training". **`?parity=run`** keeps the exact digest — background, one at a time, floored by `DREAM_PARITY_MIN_GAP_MS` (default 30 min), reporting its own `costMs`. **`?parity=`** reads both cached verdicts free. **7/7 harness cases on the real mixin:** identical→MATCH; **a CPU copy at 1/5 training→DIVERGENT with `cpuOverGpu` 0.2000, the exact signature the `% 5` shadow would leave**; nnz mismatch→STALE; not-held→STALE; no donor→UNKNOWN; f32 rounding→MATCH; no CPU matrix→UNKNOWN.
- ⛔ **Found and fixed en route — a yield cadence that was never a cadence.** The digest yielded on `(i & (CHUNK - 1)) === (CHUNK - 1)` with `CHUNK = 1_000_000`: the power-of-two mask idiom applied to a decimal constant. 999,999 is `0xF423F`, twelve bits set, so the test means *"i has all twelve of those bits set"* — about 1 step in 4,096, and clustered (999999, 1000063, 1000127, 1000191, 1000255, verified empirically). Over 1.8 billion steps that is **~440,000 yields where ~1,700 were intended**, each paying the event loop's full backlog. Now `1 << 20`. Hash output unchanged; the cadence governs only when the walk gets its slot back.

### 2026-08-30 — REBINDWAIT.1 CLOSED: the cause was mine, and I had already talked myself out of it once

Gee (verbatim): *"okay she is back up, training i guess its just a waiting game then till we can do those checks?"* → *"boom!"* → *"write it up then"*

**It was not a waiting game and it was not the donor.** `SHADOWCOST.3` added `case 'readback_matrix_values_ack'` **with its own body IN THE MIDDLE of a seven-label fall-through chain**, severing **SIX** labels from the pending-resolve body they shared and routing them into the readback settler:

```
case 'sparse_upload_ack':          ← severed
case 'sparse_propagate_ack':       ← severed
case 'sparse_hebbian_ack':         ← severed
case 'rebind_sparse_ack':          ← severed
case 'readback_letter_buckets_ack':← severed
case 'letter_surprise_ack':        ← severed
case 'readback_matrix_checksum_ack': { ...resolve the pending... }
```

Every severed pending **never resolved and rode its full timeout** — which is precisely the 16 rebinds × 30 s ≈ 8 minutes of dead boot, with every cross-projection dropped to the degraded standalone path. ⛔ **And it was never only the rebinds:** `readback_letter_buckets` (gate probes, motor argmax) and `letter_surprise` (episode salience) broke identically and said nothing, because a timeout on those lanes has no loud line. The rebind failures were merely the ones that shout.

**Fix + verification.** The case moved BELOW the block. The chain is verified **byte-identical to the pre-regression tree (`349ec380~1`) across all seven labels**, and a scan of the entire file confirms it is the ONLY fall-through chain in it. ⭐ **Live on `8dada846`:** `rebinding 16 cortex cross-projections` — **one line, sixteen silent successes**, `timeouts anywhere in the ring: 0`, `cortexCluster._cortexFullyReady = true`, `donorAppVersion='0.3.36'`, and **teaching in progress at 3.6 min against 11–12 min on the two broken boots.**

⚠ **WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT.** A fall-through chain is *syntactically identical* whether it is intact or hijacked. Inserting a case with a body between labels and their body is perfectly valid JavaScript that silently reroutes six message types — `node --check` cannot see it, ESM `import()` cannot see it, and no harness could, because the switch lives inside a live WebSocket handler. A DO-NOT-INSERT-HERE warning now sits at the chain head naming this exact failure. **The generalisable trap: adding a `case` to a `switch` is only safe at the END of a body, never between a label and the body it shares.**

⛔⛔ **THE PROCESS LESSON, AND IT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** I suspected my own build first — correctly. I could not find the mechanism, so I **traded the suspicion for a comfortable verdict**, telling Gee it was "not established" and probably pre-existing, and citing as support a previous-boot console snapshot **I had myself already labelled as taken too early to mean anything**. That is worse than having no verdict at all: it retired a live, correct lead and pointed the next investigation at the donor. **The rule earned: when you suspect your own change and cannot find the mechanism, keep looking for the mechanism — do not promote "unestablished" to "pre-existing."** The honest form of that message would have been *"I suspect my change, I cannot yet name how"* — which is exactly what I had, and exactly what I should have said.
